---
title: "AEDC: Australian Early Development Census"
description: "Information from the AEDC, a nationwide collection of early childhood development at the time children commence their first year of full-time school."
---

Information from the AEDC, a nationwide collection of early childhood development at the time children commence their first year of full-time school.

*Explains the national census, covered children, five development domains and collection method.*

banded, as the teacher reported it on the AvEDI. The dictionary defines the item as a \"Variable to indicate how many days the child has been absent from school since the beginning of the school year\", asked as \"How many days has this child been absent since the start of the year\". A1A to A1D on the same row split that absence by reason but are yes-or-no flags, not a decomposition of the band. A1 is not one of the items the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, so it never enters the PHYS score.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Days absent since the start of the year","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC absence band (four categories)","def":"A single-digit integer in four bands: 1 for 0 to 1 day, 2 for 2 to 5 days, 3 for 6 to 10 days, 4 for greater than 10 days. The entry publishes no missing-data codes, and its one-character field format leaves no room for the 88 and 99 conventions the dictionary applies to the wider AvEDI item set.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It cannot give a day count, and its lowest band merges a child who never missed a day with one who missed a single day; A1Z, present only from the 2018 cycle, is the item that separates them. Absence is also counted up to the day the teacher completed the instrument rather than over a full school year, so a child assessed in May and a child assessed in November are not on the same denominator.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":0},{"n":"A10","d":"The teacher's rating of how well the child manages stairs, used in the AvEDI as a gross motor observation.","full":"The teacher's rating of how well the child manages stairs, used in the AvEDI as a gross motor observation. The dictionary gives the purpose as \"To rate how well the child can climb stairs\" and the instrument text as \"How would you rate this child's ability to climb stairs\". It sits with A7, A8 and A9 in the physical health and wellbeing domain, and is the only one of them that depends on a particular feature of the school building.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A10","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Climbs stairs","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A10","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A don't-know answer here often means the school is single storey rather than that the child is unobserved, so the missing pattern is a property of the building and can correlate with remoteness and school size. The item also cannot detect a mobility aid or a physical disability; the D-series items in the AEDC special needs table carry that.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":1},{"n":"A11","d":"The teacher's rating of how much energy the child sustains across the school day.","full":"The teacher's rating of how much energy the child sustains across the school day. The instrument asks \"How would you rate this child's level of energy throughout the school day\", which makes it a judgement about stamina over a whole day rather than about activity at one moment. It counts towards the physical health and wellbeing domain score and is the graded companion to A3, which asks only whether the child has arrived too tired or sick.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A11","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Level of energy","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A11","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"High energy is scored as good, so the scale rewards a child who is lively and penalises a quiet or withdrawn one, which means the column cannot be read as an inattention or hyperactivity measure; the EMOT_4 sub-domain, hyperactive and inattentive behaviour, covers that. It also gives no clue whether low energy comes from sleep, nutrition, illness or a long journey to school.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":1},{"n":"A12","d":"The teacher's overall impression of the child's physical development, asked as a single summary judgement rather than a specific skill.","full":"The teacher's overall impression of the child's physical development, asked as a single summary judgement rather than a specific skill. The dictionary gives the purpose as \"To rate the child's overall physical development\", and the item enters the physical health and wellbeing domain score alongside the eleven specific items A2 to A11 and A13. It is the only item in section A that asks the teacher to generalise.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A12","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Overall physical","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A12","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is not a substitute for the PHYS domain score, even though both summarise the same territory: PHYS is calculated from the whole item set under a licensed methodology, while this is one teacher's global impression scored on three levels. Nothing physical is measured behind it, so it carries no height, weight or health information.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":1},{"n":"A13","d":"The teacher's rating of the child's day-to-day personal hygiene, on the same three-point scale as A8 to A12.","full":"The teacher's rating of the child's day-to-day personal hygiene, on the same three-point scale as A8 to A12. It is the last of the twelve items the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, and pairs with A5 on toileting and A2 on dress as the items about how a child arrives and looks after themselves rather than about motor skill. The instrument asks simply \"How would you rate this child's daily personal hygiene\".","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A13","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Daily personal hygiene","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A13","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is a teacher's assessment against an unstated standard, so it can track household resources, cultural expectations or the teacher's own norms as readily as the child's development, and the AEDC publishes no guidance on where the boundary between average and poor sits. It is not evidence of neglect and should not be used as a proxy for one.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":1},{"n":"A1A","d":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year was for family or cultural reasons, in the teacher's judgement.","full":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year was for family or cultural reasons, in the teacher's judgement. The dictionary's purpose statement is \"To identify, to the best of the teacher's knowledge, how many days the child was absent due to family/cultural obligations, including ceremonies and funerals\", and the instrument asks for an approximate number of days. It is one of four reason items, with A1B for illness or injury, A1C for other explained reasons and A1D for unexplained reasons, all sitting beside the total band in A1.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1a","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family or cultural obligations","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason flag (zero days against one or more)","def":"A single-digit integer reduced to two states, 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more days, so the day count the teacher supplied is not retained. The 2012 cycle revised the item wording; the dictionary records the end of null values against A1B rather than against this item.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1a","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It carries no volume, so a child absent once for a funeral and a child absent for a fortnight of ceremonies are the same value, and the four reason flags cannot be added up to reproduce the band in A1. The reason is also the teacher's attribution rather than the family's, so an absence the school never had explained to it lands in A1D instead.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"A1AZ","d":"The family or cultural absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1A.","full":"The family or cultural absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1A. Its purpose is given as \"To identify, to the best of the teacher's knowledge, how many days the child was absent due to family/cultural obligations, including ceremonies and funerals\". The dictionary records it as introduced in 2018, which is why it appears from the 2018 cycle table onwards and not in 2009, 2012 or 2015.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1az","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Original system: to the best of your knowledge approximately how many days absent were due to family/cultural obligations","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason item, original-system form","def":"A single-digit integer. The dictionary publishes a field format for this item but no code frame, so the categories are not documented; the flag version A1A uses 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1az","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Its categories cannot be assumed to match A1A's, because the dictionary prints no field values for the original-system reason items, so a join or a recode between the two has to be checked against the observed distribution first. Only three of the six cycles carry it, so it cannot anchor a change over the life of the census.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":3},{"n":"A1B","d":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year was put down to illness or injury.","full":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year was put down to illness or injury. The dictionary describes it as \"A variable to identify how many days the child has been absent from school due to illness / injury\", asked of the teacher as an approximate number of days and published as a flag. It sits with A1A, A1C and A1D as the four reason splits of the total absence band in A1, and it is the only one of the four that speaks to the child's health.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1b","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Illness or injury","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason flag (zero days against one or more)","def":"A single-digit integer, 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more days. The dictionary records that the item was renamed from A2a in 2012 and that null values were no longer allowed from that cycle.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1b","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is not a morbidity measure: it registers absence the school attributed to sickness, so a chronically ill child kept in class and a child kept home for one cold both resolve to 1. It also has nothing to say about the illness itself, which the D-series special needs and diagnosis items in the AEDC special needs table carry instead.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"A1BZ","d":"The illness or injury absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1B.","full":"The illness or injury absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1B. The dictionary describes it as \"A variable to identify how many days the child has been absent from school due to illness / injury\" and records it as introduced in 2018. It appears only from the 2018 cycle table, so health-related absence before that has to be taken from A1B.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1bz","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Original system: to the best of your knowledge approximately how many days absent were due to illness/injury","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason item, original-system form","def":"A single-digit integer. The dictionary gives a field format for this item but no field values, unlike A1B, which is documented as 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1bz","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is not interchangeable with A1B even though both ask the same question, because the dictionary documents no categories here, so treating the two as one series risks reading an undocumented code as a count of days. It also says nothing about the illness, which the special needs and diagnosis items in the AEDC special needs table carry.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":3},{"n":"A1C","d":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year had a reason the school knew about that was neither health nor family or cultural obligation.","full":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year had a reason the school knew about that was neither health nor family or cultural obligation. The 2009 wording the dictionary reproduces gives the examples \"Climatic conditions, financial\", which is the clearest guide to what the residual category holds. It is the third of the four reason flags, and the pair to watch is A1C against A1D: the same absence is explained in one and unexplained in the other depending only on whether the family told the school.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1c","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Other explained reasons","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason flag (zero days against one or more)","def":"A single-digit integer, 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more days. The dictionary records that the item was renamed from A3a in 2012 and that the 2009 wording listed climatic and financial reasons as examples.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1c","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is defined by what the other three flags are not, so its meaning shifts with local practice, and a school that codes weather closures here while another codes them as unexplained will differ for reasons that have nothing to do with the child. It also cannot be read as a hardship indicator, because the 2009 examples name financial reasons only as one instance among several.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"A1CZ","d":"The residual explained-absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1C.","full":"The residual explained-absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1C. The dictionary defines the reason as \"other explained reasons\", which its 2009 note for the flag version illustrates with climatic and financial circumstances. It was introduced in 2018 and appears only on the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1cz","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Other explained reasons","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason item, original-system form","def":"A single-digit integer. No field values are published for this item, so its categories are undocumented; the flag version A1C uses 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1cz","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Because the category is defined as whatever the other three reasons are not, a change in this column across cycles can reflect how schools sorted an absence rather than any change in absence itself. The undocumented code frame compounds that, so it should not be pooled with A1C without checking the observed values.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":3},{"n":"A1D","d":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year was never explained to the school.","full":"Whether any of the child's absence this school year was never explained to the school. The dictionary describes it as \"A variable to identify how many days the child has been absent from school due to un-explained reasons\", to the best of the teacher's knowledge. Of the four reason flags this is the one usually read as a risk marker, because it records a gap in contact between the family and the school rather than a stated cause.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1d","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unexplained reasons","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason flag (zero days against one or more)","def":"A single-digit integer, 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more days. The dictionary records that the item was renamed from A4a in 2012.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1d","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It measures what the school was told, not why the child was away, so a family that does not ring in and a family with no reason to keep the child home produce the same value. A single unexplained day sets the flag, which makes it a poor proxy for chronic non-attendance; the total band in A1 is the only volume information on the row.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"A1DZ","d":"The unexplained-absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1D.","full":"The unexplained-absence question on the older response scale the AEDC dictionary calls the original system, carried alongside the flag version in A1D. The dictionary's purpose statement is \"To identify, to the best of the teacher's knowledge, how many days the child was absent due to unexplained reasons\". Like the other original-system reason items it appears only on the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables, so it covers the last three cycles of the census.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1dz","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unexplained reasons","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI absence-reason item, original-system form","def":"A single-digit integer with no field values published in the dictionary. The corresponding flag version A1D is documented as 0 for zero days and 1 for one or more.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1dz","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It records the absence of an explanation reaching the school, not truancy, and cannot separate a family that does not report from one the school failed to record. Its codes are undocumented and its coverage starts at the 2018 cycle, so it cannot be used to test whether unexplained absence changed since the 2009 baseline.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":3},{"n":"A1Z","d":"The same absence question as A1 but on the older, finer response scale that the AEDC dictionary labels the original system.","full":"The same absence question as A1 but on the older, finer response scale that the AEDC dictionary labels the original system. It matters because it is the only column that separates a child with no absence at all from a child with one day: A1 folds both into a single band, while this item keeps 0 days and 1 day apart on a five-point scale. The dictionary gives its instrument text as \"How many days has this child been absent since the start of the year\" and records it as introduced in 2018, which is why it appears from the 2018 cycle table onwards.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A1z","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Original system: how many days has this child been absent since the start of the year","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC absence band, original-system five-category form","def":"A single-digit integer over five categories: 0 for 0 days, 1 for 1 day, 2 for 2 to 5 days, 3 for 6 to 10 days and 4 for greater than 10 days. Its codes also only partly line up with A1's: 2, 3 and 4 carry the same bands in both, but A1's code 1 covers 0 to 1 day while here code 1 is exactly one day and code 0 holds the children with no absence at all, so pooling the two columns without recoding puts every zero-absence child in the wrong band.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":4},{"n":"A2","d":"Whether the child has turned up to school over- or under-dressed more than once this year, in the teacher's judgement.","full":"Whether the child has turned up to school over- or under-dressed more than once this year, in the teacher's judgement. The instrument asks \"Since the start of the year, has the child sometimes (more than once) arrived over or under-dressed for school related activities\". It is one of the twelve items, A2 to A13, that the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, and one of the four (with A3, A4 and A5) that reads as a marker of how well a child arrives ready for the day rather than of motor skill.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A2","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dressed inappropriately","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 yes, 2 no, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for yes, 2 for no and 88 for don't know, so a low code is the adverse answer here.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A2","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The coding direction is the opposite of A5, A6, A7 and B10 to B19, which use 1 for no and 2 for yes, so summing raw codes across a section mixes problems with strengths. The item also says nothing about why a child is dressed as they are, and a single occasion does not register at all, since the question sets its threshold at more than once.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A3","d":"Whether the child has arrived too tired or too sick to do schoolwork more than once this year.","full":"Whether the child has arrived too tired or too sick to do schoolwork more than once this year. The instrument combines the two states in one question: \"Since the start of the year, has the child sometimes (more than once) arrived too tired and/or too sick to do schoolwork\". A3A and A3B split it into tiredness and sickness, but the dictionary records that they are only answered when this item is yes, so this is the gate on both. It counts towards the physical health and wellbeing domain score, which its two follow-ups do not.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A3","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Too tired and/or sick","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 yes, 2 no, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for yes, 2 for no and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A3","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A yes cannot be read as a health signal on its own, because the question fuses fatigue with illness and only the follow-up items separate them; and those follow-ups are missing for New South Wales in the first two cycles. Its threshold of more than once also means an isolated bad morning leaves no trace.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A3A","d":"Whether tiredness in particular is behind a yes on A3, asked only of children whose teacher already said they arrived too tired or too sick.","full":"Whether tiredness in particular is behind a yes on A3, asked only of children whose teacher already said they arrived too tired or too sick. The dictionary states the filter plainly as \"Only answer if A3 = Yes\", and records that the item was \"Not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1/2\". Unlike A3 it is not one of the items the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, so it informs interpretation rather than the score.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A3a","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Too tired","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 yes, 2 no, 88 don't know), filtered","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for yes, 2 for no and 88 for don't know, populated only where A3 is yes.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A3a","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A blank does not mean the child is well rested; it usually means the gate question was answered no, or that the child was in New South Wales in 2009 or 2012 when the item was not collected. A national count of tired children taken from this column therefore undercounts, and until the 2015 filter revision the item was asked of all non-NSW students, so the denominator is not the same across cycles.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A3B","d":"Whether sickness in particular is behind a yes on A3, asked only of children whose teacher already said they arrived too tired or too sick.","full":"Whether sickness in particular is behind a yes on A3, asked only of children whose teacher already said they arrived too tired or too sick. The instrument wording is \"Since the start of the year, has the child sometimes (more than once) arrived too sick to do schoolwork\", and the dictionary applies the same \"Only answer if A3 = Yes\" filter and the same New South Wales exclusion for Cycles 1 and 2 as A3A. A child can be yes on both this item and A3A, so the two do not partition the A3 population.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A3b","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Too sick","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 yes, 2 no, 88 don't know), filtered","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for yes, 2 for no and 88 for don't know, populated only where A3 is yes.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A3b","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It records a teacher's impression of a child in class, not a medical judgement, so it neither confirms an illness nor rules one out for a child kept home instead, whose absence lands in A1B. Blanks are dominated by the A3 filter and the missing New South Wales collections, so the column cannot be treated as a national yes-or-no on illness at school.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A4","d":"Whether the child has arrived at school hungry more than once this year, in the teacher's judgement.","full":"Whether the child has arrived at school hungry more than once this year, in the teacher's judgement. The dictionary's purpose is \"To identify if, since the start of the year, the child has arrived hungry at school on more than one occasion\", and the item counts towards the physical health and wellbeing domain score. A4A on the 2018 and later core tables records whether the child attends a breakfast club, which is the service-side companion to this question.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A4","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hungry","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 yes, 2 no, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for yes, 2 for no and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A4","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is not a measure of food insecurity: it captures what a teacher noticed in a classroom, so a child fed at a breakfast club before class can be recorded as not hungry while the household situation is unchanged. Because a yes needs more than one occasion, it also cannot flag an acute episode.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A4A","d":"Whether the child attends a breakfast club run by the school or the community.","full":"Whether the child attends a breakfast club run by the school or the community. The dictionary describes it as a \"Variable to indicate if the child attends school/community breakfast club\", and it appears in PLIDA only from the 2018 cycle because it was renamed from D12 that year. The 2024 cycle applied \"Consistent business rules ... across Cycles to ensure concordance between School Coordinator and Teacher responses for a school\", so the answer is reconciled against what the school itself reported from 2015 onwards.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A4a","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Does the child attend a school/community breakfast club","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item with not-applicable (0 no, 1 yes, 88, 99)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 0 for no, 1 for yes, 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable, the last added in 2015.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A4a","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It cannot be read as a child-level exposure to a nutrition programme, because it partly reflects whether the school runs a club at all and has been reconciled to the school coordinator's answer; 99 marks the cases where the question does not arise rather than a child who declined. The instrument asks \"Would you say this child is independent in toileting habits most of the time\", and the dictionary counts the item towards the physical health and wellbeing domain score. It is coded the opposite way round to A2, A3 and A4: here the higher code, 2, is the positive answer.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A5","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Washroom","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know, so the direction is reversed relative to the yes-first items earlier in section A.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A5","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is a judgement about classroom independence, not a clinical statement about continence, and the qualifier 'most of the time' means an occasional accident does not move the answer. The AEDC also does not compute domain categories for children diagnosed with special needs, so this item cannot be used to profile the children for whom toileting support is most likely to be an issue.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A6","d":"Whether the child has settled on one hand rather than swapping, in the teacher's judgement.","full":"Whether the child has settled on one hand rather than swapping, in the teacher's judgement. The instrument asks \"Would you say this child shows an established hand preference (right vs. left or vice versa)\", so the answer is about whether a preference exists, not which hand it is. It is one of the twelve items the dictionary allocates to the physical health and wellbeing domain, where an established preference is treated as a marker of fine motor development.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hand preference","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It cannot identify left-handed children: both a left-handed and a right-handed child answer yes, and the AvEDI collects no column recording which hand. It is the gross motor counterpart to A8 and A9, which rate pen grip and object handling, and all three feed the physical health and wellbeing domain score.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A7","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Well coordinated","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know, in the same direction as A5, A6 and the B-series literacy items.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A7","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is a single yes-or-no on whole-body movement, so it cannot grade coordination or separate a mild clumsiness from a motor impairment; the three-point items A10 and A12 are the nearest thing to a gradient. A yes also does not mean the child was assessed under comparable conditions, since teachers observe children in very different play spaces.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"A8","d":"The teacher's rating of how well the child holds a pen, crayon or brush.","full":"The teacher's rating of how well the child holds a pen, crayon or brush. It is a fine motor item in the physical health and wellbeing domain, and the closest physical companion to the writing items B18 to B23 in the language and cognitive domain.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A8","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficient at holding pen","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know. Both ends of the scale carry a merged label, code 1 covering poor and very poor and code 3 covering good and very good, so the extremes cannot be separated.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A8","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It cannot separate a grip problem from a lack of practice, since a child who has rarely held a pencil and a child with a motor difficulty both rate poor. The merged top and bottom categories also mean the column cannot identify the very poorest or very best writers, which matters if the intent is to find children needing occupational therapy referral.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":1},{"n":"A9","d":"The teacher's rating of how well the child handles objects, on the same three-point scale as A8, A10, A11, A12 and A13.","full":"The teacher's rating of how well the child handles objects, on the same three-point scale as A8, A10, A11, A12 and A13. The instrument asks \"How would you rate this child's ability to manipulate objects\" without naming particular objects, so the teacher applies it to whatever the classroom offers. It is one of the fine motor items in the physical health and wellbeing domain.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A9","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Manipulates objects","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry A9","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The question names no task, so the rating is anchored to the materials and expectations of one classroom rather than to a fixed standard, which makes it weaker for comparing individual children than for comparing large groups. It also overlaps heavily with A8, so treating the two as independent evidence of fine motor skill double counts one judgement.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":1},{"n":"AGCAMPUSID","d":"The Commonwealth's own code for the school campus at which the child was assessed.","full":"The Commonwealth's own code for the school campus at which the child was assessed. The dictionary defines it as \"The individual campus code used by the Australian Government to identify each school campus participating in the AEDC\", held on the Master Unit Record File and \"Suppressed for schools outside of a data recipient's jurisdiction\". It appears in PLIDA only on the 2018 cycle table, because the dictionary records the item being replaced by AGLocationID from 2021 and fully discontinued in 2024.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AGCampusID","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"National campus identifier used by deewr","k":"Australian Government school campus identifier","def":"A five-digit integer allocated by the Australian Government, not a serial within the AEDC file, so the value range is set by the national school register rather than by this collection.","p":"2018","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AGCampusID","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It cannot follow a school across cycles in PLIDA, since only the 2018 table carries it and its successors sit under different names; SCHOOLID is the identifier present in every cycle. It also identifies a campus, not a school or a teacher, so a multi-campus school splits across values while TEACHERID separates classes within a campus.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core"]},{"n":"AGECAT","d":"The finest published banding of the child's age, in steps of roughly three months across the school-entry range.","full":"The finest published banding of the child's age, in steps of roughly three months across the school-entry range. It is a derived variable, built from the age the dictionary describes as \"based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher\". AGECUT, AGEGROUP and AGEGROUP3TO7 on the same row are coarser cuts of the same underlying age, and AGEINMONTHS is the ungrouped version.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCat","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age categories (15 narrow)","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC narrow age band (16 categories)","def":"A two-digit integer from 0 to 15, so sixteen codes despite the name; the '15 narrow' in the custodian's label counts the non-zero codes. Codes 1 to 13 step in roughly three-month intervals from 3 years 8 months to 6 years 10 months; code 0 is everything under 3 years 8 months, code 14 spans 6 years 10 months to 7 years 6 months, and code 15 is everything above.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCat","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The bands are not equal width, so treating the code as a linear age scale compresses the middle and stretches both tails, and a regression on the raw code will not recover a per-month effect. Age is also measured at the day the teacher completed the instrument rather than at a fixed census date, so two children on the same code were assessed at different points in the school year.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":7},{"n":"AGECUT","d":"The coarsest numeric grouping of the child's age, splitting the cohort into under five, five, and six or older.","full":"The coarsest numeric grouping of the child's age, splitting the cohort into under five, five, and six or older. The dictionary marks it as derived and gives its purpose as \"A grouping variable for child age\", which is what it is normally used for: a control or a cross-tabulation axis when the sixteen bands of AGECAT are too fine. AGEGROUP holds the same idea as text with the top group cut at seven rather than six.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCut","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age categories (3 broad)","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC broad age band (three categories)","def":"A single-digit integer with three codes: 0 for under 5 years, 1 for 5 years and 2 for 6 years and older.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeCut","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Its top and bottom categories are open, so a four-year-old and a three-year-old share code 0 while a six-year-old and an eight-year-old share code 2, which hides exactly the age spread that matters when comparing schools with different entry rules. The bottom category also mixes children the AEDC excludes from domain categories, those under four years, with four-year-olds who are scored.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":8},{"n":"AGEGROUP","d":"The confidentialised age grouping the AEDC uses in its published outputs, held as text rather than as a code.","full":"The confidentialised age grouping the AEDC uses in its published outputs, held as text rather than as a code. Section 4.4 of the dictionary says the age variable is \"available in years and is confidentialised as follows\" and then lists under five years, five years, six years and over six years, and this is the column that carries that grouping. AGECUT expresses almost the same split numerically, but its top band starts at six while this one holds six-year-olds separately and reserves its top value for seven and over.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age group","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC confidentialised age group (text)","def":"A two-character text field with four values: '<5' for under 5 years, '5' for 5 to under 6, '6' for 6 to under 7, and '>6' for 7 years and over. The field is left justified, not numeric.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Two of its four values are not numbers, so converting the column to numeric silently drops the youngest and oldest children to missing and leaves an apparently clean five-and-six-year-old sample that is missing its tails. The label '>6' is also misleading on its own, since the dictionary defines it as age 7 years or more rather than anything above six.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":9},{"n":"AGEGROUP3TO7","d":"The child's age in completed years at the time the teacher filled in the instrument, held as a plain integer from 3 to 7.","full":"The child's age in completed years at the time the teacher filled in the instrument, held as a plain integer from 3 to 7. It is the numeric age variable most convenient for analysis on the AEDC core tables, and the dictionary marks it as derived rather than reported. AGEINMONTHS is the finer version of the same quantity, AGECAT the finer banding, and AGEGROUP the text grouping used for publication.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup3to7","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age in years","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC age in completed years, top coded at 7","def":"A single-digit integer taking 3 for age 3 to under 4, 4 for 4 to under 5, 5 for 5 to under 6, 6 for 6 to under 7, and 7 for 7 and over. Only the top code is open; the others are exact one-year intervals.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeGroup3to7","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Its name suggests a range of three to seven, but code 7 is a top code with no upper bound, so an eight-year-old repeating a year is indistinguishable from a child who has just turned seven. Rounding down to completed years also loses up to eleven months of development, which is large relative to the age effects the AEDC domain cut-offs are designed to absorb.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":10},{"n":"AGEINMONTHS","d":"The child's age in whole months when the teacher completed the instrument, and the finest age measure on the AEDC file.","full":"The child's age in whole months when the teacher completed the instrument, and the finest age measure on the AEDC file. The dictionary marks it as derived and section 4.4 explains the derivation: \"AEDC age is based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher.\" Every other age column on the row, AGECAT, AGECUT, AGEGROUP and AGEGROUP3TO7, is a banding of this quantity.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeInMonths","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Age in months","k":"Age in completed months","def":"A three-digit integer counting completed months, so a child of five years and three months is 63. There is no code frame; the domain is open across the school-entry age range.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry AgeInMonths","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is age at assessment, not age at a common reference date, so it moves with when in the school year the teacher happened to complete the instrument as much as with the child's date of birth; MOC, the month of completion, is the column needed to adjust for that. It also cannot be turned back into a date of birth, which is not released.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"ARRIVALYEAR","d":"The year the child first came to Australia, asked on the instrument as \"In which year did the child first arrive in Australia\".","full":"The year the child first came to Australia, asked on the instrument as \"In which year did the child first arrive in Australia\". Read against AGEINMONTHS it gives an approximate age at migration, and against COUNTRY and PLACEOFBIRTH on the same row it distinguishes a child born overseas who arrived as an infant from one who arrived shortly before starting school. The dictionary records the item as introduced in 2015, which is why it is absent from the 2009 and 2012 cycle tables.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ArrivalYear","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year of arrival","k":"Year of first arrival in Australia (four-digit year, 9999 unknown)","def":"A four-digit integer holding a calendar year, with 9999 reserved for unknown. There is no separate not-applicable code for children born in Australia.","p":"2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ArrivalYear","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The 9999 sentinel is a valid four-digit year to any arithmetic, so a mean or a difference computed without excluding it is badly wrong. It also records the first arrival, so a child who left and returned is dated by the earlier trip, and it says nothing about visa status or whether the family arrived together.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"ATSI","d":"Whether the child is recorded as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, the gate on every other item in the AEDC Indigenous table.","full":"Whether the child is recorded as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, the gate on every other item in the AEDC Indigenous table. The dictionary defines it as follows: \"A child is considered to be 'Indigenous' if he or she identifies as being of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin. The term 'origin' is considered to relate to people's Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent and for some, but not all, their cultural identity.\" ATSITYPE beside it splits Aboriginal from Torres Strait Islander origin, and B1A to B1D rate the child's use of Aboriginal English, Kriol and traditional languages.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSI","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous status (1 representing indigenous null signifying non-indigenous/non-identifying)","k":"Indigenous status (Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin)","def":"A single-digit integer, documented by the AEDC as 0 for no and 1 for yes. The PLIDA data item list describes the field differently, as 1 for Indigenous with null signifying non-Indigenous or non-identifying, so the negative case may arrive as missing rather than as zero.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSI","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The two published descriptions disagree on how a non-Indigenous child is stored, so a test written as ATSI equals 0 can return nobody while ATSI equals 1 works; check the observed values before building a denominator. The item is also a school enrolment record of origin rather than a self-report by the child or family at census time, and 'not identifying' is indistinguishable from 'not Indigenous' in either coding.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2009 / aedc_2009_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2012 / aedc_2012_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2015 / aedc_2015_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2018 / aedc_2018_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2021 / aedc_2021_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2024 / aedc_2024_ind"]},{"n":"ATSITYPE","d":"Which Indigenous origin the child is recorded as having, asked only where ATSI on the same row is yes.","full":"Which Indigenous origin the child is recorded as having, asked only where ATSI on the same row is yes. The dictionary states the filter as \"Only answer if ATSI = Yes\" and the jurisdictional rule as \"Not provided in New South Wales\", with a 2015 filter revision noting that previous cycles did not include NSW students at all. Its purpose is to add detail rather than to change the count of Indigenous children, which ATSI alone establishes.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ATSIType","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous background","k":"Indigenous origin type (Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, both, neither, not stated)","def":"A single-digit integer with five codes: 1 Aboriginal but not Torres Strait Islander origin, 2 Torres Strait Islander but not Aboriginal origin, 3 both, 4 neither, and 9 not stated or unknown.
