Code 4, neither origin, can also appear on rows where ATSI is yes, so the two columns can contradict each other and ATSI should be the one used to define the population.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2009 / aedc_2009_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2012 / aedc_2012_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2015 / aedc_2015_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2018 / aedc_2018_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2021 / aedc_2021_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2024 / aedc_2024_ind"]},{"n":"B1","d":"The teacher's rating of how effectively the child uses English, asked as \"How would you rate this child's ability to use language effectively in English\".","full":"The teacher's rating of how effectively the child uses English, asked as \"How would you rate this child's ability to use language effectively in English\". The dictionary allocates it to the communication skills and general knowledge domain, not to language and cognitive skills, so it feeds COMGEN rather than LANGCOG. B1A to B1D in the AEDC Indigenous table carry the parallel ratings for Aboriginal English, Kriol, traditional languages and other Indigenous languages, and ESL and LANG on the core table record whether English is the home language at all.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficient in english","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point proficiency rating with not-applicable (1 poor, 2 average, 3 good, 88, 99)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for poor or very poor, 2 for average, 3 for very good or good, with 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable. It is one of the few AvEDI items to carry the not-applicable code.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A low rating is not evidence of a language delay: the item rates English specifically, so a child fluent in another language and new to English scores at the bottom on linguistic competence they in fact have. Reading it alongside LBOTE, ESL and the B1A to B1D Indigenous language ratings is the only way to tell the two situations apart.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":11},{"n":"B10","d":"Whether the child shows curiosity about printed material, asked as \"Would you say this child is interested in reading (inquisitive/curious about the meaning of printed material)?\".","full":"Whether the child shows curiosity about printed material, asked as \"Would you say this child is interested in reading (inquisitive/curious about the meaning of printed material)?\". It is one of the twenty-six items, B8 to B33, that the dictionary allocates to the language and cognitive skills domain, and it sits at the disposition end of that set: B11 to B17 test what the child can actually do with letters and words. E7 on the core table records whether the child is read to at home.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B10","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Interested in reading","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know, so the higher code is the positive answer across the whole B10 to B19 block.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B10","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It rates an attitude the teacher infers from behaviour in class, so a child who is interested in books at home but reticent at school reads as a no; it is not a measure of reading ability, which B15 to B17 carry. The binary form also gives no gradient, so it cannot separate mild from strong interest.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B11","d":"Whether the child can name at least some letters of the alphabet, the first rung of the literacy ladder in the AvEDI.","full":"Whether the child can name at least some letters of the alphabet, the first rung of the literacy ladder in the AvEDI. The instrument asks \"Would you say this child is able to identify some letters of the alphabet\", with no threshold on how many. It is a language and cognitive skills domain item and the base for B12, which asks whether the child can attach sounds to letters.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B11","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Identifies letters","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B11","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Because 'some' is undefined, the item saturates: most children in their first year of school answer yes, so it separates the very lowest group from everyone else and carries almost no information about the rest. It also does not distinguish recognising a letter shape from knowing its name or its sound.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B12","d":"Whether the child can attach sounds to letters, the phonics step between recognising letters in B11 and reading words in B15.","full":"Whether the child can attach sounds to letters, the phonics step between recognising letters in B11 and reading words in B15. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify if the child is able to attach sounds to letters\", asked of the teacher as a single yes-or-no judgement. It is one of the language and cognitive skills domain items and, with B13 on rhyming, one of the two phonological awareness questions in the instrument.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B12","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Sounds to letters","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B12","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is the teacher's impression from ordinary classroom work rather than a phonics assessment, so it will track how much explicit phonics teaching the class has done as well as the child's own skill. Nothing in the column says how many letter-sound correspondences the child knows, so it cannot be used to rank children within the yes group.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B13","d":"Whether the child notices that words rhyme, asked as \"Would you say this child is showing awareness of rhyming words\".","full":"Whether the child notices that words rhyme, asked as \"Would you say this child is showing awareness of rhyming words\". Rhyme awareness is the oral side of early literacy, so this item and B12 on letter sounds are the two phonological questions in a block otherwise concerned with print. It counts towards the language and cognitive skills domain score.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B13","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Rhyming awareness","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B13","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Rhyme is language specific, so a child whose home language is not English can show the awareness in that language and still be rated no here, which is why B1, LBOTE and ESL belong in any interpretation of a low score. The wording asks only whether awareness is showing, not whether the child can produce rhymes, so a yes sets a low bar.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B14","d":"Whether the child can take part in group reading activities, the only item in the literacy block that is about behaviour in a group rather than an individual skill.","full":"Whether the child can take part in group reading activities, the only item in the literacy block that is about behaviour in a group rather than an individual skill. The dictionary's purpose is \"To identify if the child is able to participate in group reading activities\". It counts towards the language and cognitive skills domain, but what it measures overlaps with the classroom conduct items in section C, since sitting through a shared book requires attention as much as reading.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B14","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Group reading","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B14","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It depends on the classroom running group reading at all, so a no can mean the activity does not happen rather than that the child cannot join in, and the don't-know code is the only place that shows. It also confounds reading with attention and social participation, so it should not be read as evidence about reading skill on its own.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B15","d":"Whether the child can read simple words, the first of three items that step up in difficulty through B16 for complex words and B17 for simple sentences.","full":"Whether the child can read simple words, the first of three items that step up in difficulty through B16 for complex words and B17 for simple sentences. The instrument asks \"Would you say this child is able to read simple words\", leaving 'simple' to the teacher's judgement. All three are language and cognitive skills domain items, and together they are the part of the AvEDI that discriminates among the more advanced readers at school entry.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B15","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Reads simple words","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B15","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The instrument does not enforce the ladder, so a child can be coded no here and yes on B16 or B17; the three items are not a scale and should not be summed without checking for those inconsistent patterns. What counts as a simple word is also left to the teacher, so the threshold moves between classrooms.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B16","d":"Whether the child can read complex words, the middle rung between simple words in B15 and simple sentences in B17.","full":"Whether the child can read complex words, the middle rung between simple words in B15 and simple sentences in B17. The dictionary's purpose statement is \"To identify if the child is able to read complex words\", with no definition of complexity offered to the teacher. It is a language and cognitive skills domain item and, being a yes for only a minority of children at school entry, one of the items that does most to separate advanced readers.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B16","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Reads complex words","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B16","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Complexity is undefined in the instrument, so the teacher supplies the standard and the item cannot be benchmarked against any external reading level or against NAPLAN later on. Because few children score yes, small changes in teacher interpretation move the national rate more than they would for a common item like B11.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B17","d":"Whether the child can read simple sentences, the top of the three reading items in the AvEDI.","full":"Whether the child can read simple sentences, the top of the three reading items in the AvEDI. The dictionary's data element description reads \"Variable to indicate if the child reads sentences\", with the instrument asking specifically about simple sentences. A yes marks a child already reading connected text in their first year of school, which is why this item and B16 carry most of the weight at the strong end of the language and cognitive skills domain.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B17","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Reads sentences","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B17","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It records decoding, not comprehension: the question asks whether the child can read the sentence, not whether they understood it, and no item in the instrument covers understanding of connected text. A no is also the normal answer for children starting school, so it should not be treated as a difficulty marker on its own.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B18","d":"Whether the child plays with writing tools, the first of the writing items that run through to B23.","full":"Whether the child plays with writing tools, the first of the writing items that run through to B23. The dictionary's purpose is \"To identify if the child is experimenting with writing tools\", so the criterion is willingness to try rather than any product. It counts towards the language and cognitive skills domain, and the physical companion is A8, which rates how well the child actually holds a pen, crayon or brush.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B18","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Experiments writing","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B18","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Experimenting with a pencil is not writing, so a yes says nothing about whether the child can form letters, which B21 to B23 ask. Access matters too: a classroom or home with few materials suppresses the behaviour without any difference in the child's development.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B19","d":"Whether the child knows which way English is written on a page, asked as \"Would you say this child is aware of writing directions in English (left to right, top to bottom)\".","full":"Whether the child knows which way English is written on a page, asked as \"Would you say this child is aware of writing directions in English (left to right, top to bottom)\". It is a concepts-of-print item rather than a writing skill: it tests orientation, which typically precedes forming letters in B21 to B23. It counts towards the language and cognitive skills domain score.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B19","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Writing directions","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI yes-or-no item (1 no, 2 yes, 88 don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer coded 1 for no, 2 for yes and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry B19","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The item is tied to English orthography, so a child already literate in a right-to-left or vertically written script is recorded as unaware of writing direction when in fact they hold a different convention; nothing in the AvEDI records that. It also tests knowledge of the page, not handwriting, so a yes carries no information about legibility.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom"],"dom":5},{"n":"B1A","d":"A teacher's rating of how well the child uses Aboriginal English in the classroom or playground, asked as one of four language options under item B1.","full":"A teacher's rating of how well the child uses Aboriginal English in the classroom or playground, asked as one of four language options under item B1. The data dictionary gives the instrument wording as \"How would you rate this child's ability to use languages other than Standard Australian English effectively in the classroom / playground: Aboriginal English (AE)\". It sits in aedc_2009_ind beside ATSI, ATSITYPE and the Indigenous language identifiers, and from the 2015 cycle it is only asked when ATSITYPE records the child as Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander or both; in earlier cycles it was asked of every student outside New South Wales.","dsrc":"Australian Early Development Census Data Dictionary, version 5.0 (March 2019), Australian Government Department of Education and Training","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/resources/aedc-data-dictionary-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=be6148a0_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Aboriginal English (AE)","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point ability rating","def":"A single integer on the AvEDI rating scale: 1 poor or very poor, 2 average, 3 very good or good. The AEDC-wide missing conventions apply on top of that, so 88 is don't know and 99 is not applicable.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Early Development Census Data Dictionary, version 5.0 (March 2019), Australian Government Department of Education and Training","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/resources/aedc-data-dictionary-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=be6148a0_1","lim":"It rates a teacher's judgement of ability, not whether the child actually speaks Aboriginal English, and a teacher who does not speak the variety may record 88 rather than a low score. A blank cannot be read as 'no ability' either, because the item was never fielded in New South Wales in cycles 1 and 2 and is filtered on Indigenous status from 2015. It also feeds no domain score: only B1 counts towards communication skills and general knowledge.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2009 / aedc_2009_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2012 / aedc_2012_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2015 / aedc_2015_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2018 / aedc_2018_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2021 / aedc_2021_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2024 / aedc_2024_ind"],"dom":11},{"n":"B1B","d":"A teacher's rating of how well the child uses Kriol or Creole in the classroom or playground, the second of the four language options under item B1.","full":"A teacher's rating of how well the child uses Kriol or Creole in the classroom or playground, the second of the four language options under item B1. The data dictionary describes it as a \"Variable to indicate the child's ability to use Kriol/Creole\", rated on the same three-point scale as the child's English proficiency in B1. Which contact language the child actually speaks is carried separately by ILANGUAGEID and OTHERILANGUAGEID1 to 3 in the same aedc_2009_ind table.","dsrc":"Australian Early Development Census Data Dictionary, version 5.0 (March 2019), Australian Government Department of Education and Training","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/resources/aedc-data-dictionary-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=be6148a0_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Kriol/Creole","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point ability rating","def":"A single integer on the AvEDI rating scale: 1 poor or very poor, 2 average, 3 very good or good. The AEDC-wide missing conventions apply on top of that, so 88 is don't know and 99 is not applicable.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Early Development Census Data Dictionary, version 5.0 (March 2019), Australian Government Department of Education and Training","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/resources/aedc-data-dictionary-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=be6148a0_1","lim":"The item pools every Kriol and creole variety into one rating, so it cannot identify the language: a child speaking Kriol in the Kimberley and a child speaking Torres Strait Creole are indistinguishable here. A rating is also not evidence that the language is spoken at home, since the teacher is judging classroom and playground use. It contributes nothing to the five domain scores.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2009 / aedc_2009_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2012 / aedc_2012_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2015 / aedc_2015_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2018 / aedc_2018_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2021 / aedc_2021_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2024 / aedc_2024_ind"],"dom":11},{"n":"B1C","d":"A teacher's rating of how well the child uses a traditional Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander language in the classroom or playground.","full":"A teacher's rating of how well the child uses a traditional Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander language in the classroom or playground. It carries the tightest filter of the four B1 language options: the dictionary records that it is only asked when ATSITYPE identifies the child as Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander or both \"and child speaks a Traditional Aboriginal Language (not Aboriginal English or Kriol)\". A blank therefore usually means the screening condition was not met rather than that the teacher skipped it.","dsrc":"Australian Early Development Census Data Dictionary, version 5.0 (March 2019), Australian Government Department of Education and Training","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/resources/aedc-data-dictionary-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=be6148a0_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Traditional ATSI language","t":"categorical","k":"AvEDI three-point ability rating","def":"A single integer on the AvEDI rating scale: 1 poor or very poor, 2 average, 3 very good or good. The AEDC-wide missing conventions apply on top of that, so 88 is don't know and 99 is not applicable.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Early Development Census Data Dictionary, version 5.0 (March 2019), Australian Government Department of Education and Training","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/resources/aedc-data-dictionary-2019.pdf?sfvrsn=be6148a0_1","lim":"It does not name the language. A single rating covers every traditional language in the country, and the language itself has to be read from ILANGUAGEID or the OTHERILANGUAGEID columns. Because the filter conditions on the child already being reported as a speaker, the rated group is not a random sample of Indigenous children, so a mean over this column is not a population estimate of traditional language ability.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2009 / aedc_2009_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2012 / aedc_2012_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2015 / aedc_2015_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2018 / aedc_2018_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2021 / aedc_2021_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2024 / aedc_2024_ind"],"dom":11},{"n":"B1D","d":"A teacher's rating of the child's ability in an Indigenous language that is not Aboriginal English, Kriol or a traditional language, the residual option under item B1.","full":"A teacher's rating of the child's ability in an Indigenous language that is not Aboriginal English, Kriol or a traditional language, the residual option under item B1. Because the AEDC is collected in a child's first year of full-time school, a Yes marks a child doing that first year a second time, which usually also means they are older than their classmates.","dsrc":"AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 9 Instrument Background","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child repeating this grade","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC yes/no grade repetition flag","def":"One integer: 0 for No and 1 for Yes.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 9 Instrument Background","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It does not say why the child is repeating, who decided, or whether the earlier year was at the same school. Age is held separately in AGEINMONTHS and the age category columns, so the flag should be read beside those rather than used as a proxy for being older than the class.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"CLASSTYPEC","d":"Whether the child was enrolled in more than one educational setting when the teacher completed the instrument.","full":"Whether the child was enrolled in more than one educational setting when the teacher completed the instrument. The AEDC defines dual placement as \"when the child is co-enrolled at two or more educational institutions, or in two or more educational programs\", and the teacher answers it for every child in the class. From the 2018 cycle CLASSTYPEC_2 sits beside it and names which kind of second placement it was, asked only where this column is 1. It matters for reading the rest of the row, because the responding teacher sees a dual-placed child for only part of their school life.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element ClassTypeC","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dual placement","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC dual placement flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes. The dictionary instructs that it is asked \"Only if ClassTypeC = Yes\", so a missing value here is the filter working rather than a teacher declining to answer. It appears in the PLIDA 2018, 2021 and 2024 core tables only, so the type of dual placement cannot be recovered for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles even though CLASSTYPEC itself runs across all six.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element ClassTypeC_2","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of dual placement","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC dual placement type","def":"A one-digit integer with three categories: 1 special education program, 2 language school, 3 other.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element ClassTypeC_2","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It records one type only, so a child co-enrolled in both a special education programme and a language school cannot be represented, and code 3 carries no free text saying what the other setting was.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":13},{"n":"COMGEN","d":"The child's score on communication skills and general knowledge, one of the five AEDC developmental domains.","full":"The child's score on communication skills and general knowledge, one of the five AEDC developmental domains. The AEDC states that its indicators \"have been developed and validated for use as a population measure at a group level and have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children\", so a low score for one child carries far less meaning than a low share across a community. The cut-offs are fixed at the 2009 baseline: the dictionary records that \"the cut-off scores used in 2009 have remained the same across each collection cycle\", so a rise in the share coded 1 is a real fall in scores rather than a moving benchmark.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 and data element COMGENCategory","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Vulnerable - communication","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain vulnerability category","def":"A one-digit integer with four bands: 1 = 0 to 10th percentile, 2 = 11th to 25th, 3 = 26th to 50th, 4 = 51st to 100th. It takes the same value on every row of a cycle's file, so its only real use is telling which vintage of the AEDC data a PLIDA table was cut from. The dictionary lists it as a derived field carried on the complete, core and linkage AEDC files and introduced in the 2012 cycle, although PLIDA carries the column in all six core tables, 2009 included.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element CreationDate","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"File creation date","k":"File creation date (10-character text)","def":"A ten-character text field holding a date. It is typed as text rather than as a date, so it sorts alphabetically unless it is parsed first.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element CreationDate","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It cannot date anything the child did. The collection year is YEAR and the month the teacher completed the instrument is MOC; using this column to order children or to work out age at assessment would substitute the file's build date for the child's own timing.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"CYCLE","d":"Which of the six triennial AEDC collections the row belongs to, numbered 1 to 6 for 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024.","full":"Which of the six triennial AEDC collections the row belongs to, numbered 1 to 6 for 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024. The dictionary defines it simply as \"The AEDC collection cycle\". It is not interchangeable with YEAR: cycle 1 spans both 2009 and 2010, and the AEDC directs that \"2010 data is excluded from all results except Community / Local Community level results\". Grouping on this column is how a PLIDA user reproduces an AEDC published figure, since every AEDC report is organised by cycle.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element Cycle, table 1 and section 2.3","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"AEDC cycle","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC collection cycle number","def":"A one-digit integer from 1 to 6, one value per collection: 1 = 2009, 2 = 2012, 3 = 2015, 4 = 2018, 5 = 2021, 6 = 2024.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element Cycle, table 1 and section 2.3","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It does not make cycles comparable. Several instrument items changed between collections, most visibly the condition items D1 to D9 which gained a separate 'yes but does not affect learning' code from cycle 3, and community boundaries were redrawn for cycle 6 and applied backwards, so a trend built by grouping on this column alone can be comparing different questions or different areas.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":16},{"n":"D1","d":"Whether the child has a physical disability and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning.","full":"Whether the child has a physical disability and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning. The AEDC's purpose for the item is \"To identify if the child has a physical disability that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom\", and it is the first of nine condition items D1 to D9 the teacher answers for every child. The code frame carries its own history: code 3 is a plain yes used only in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, while codes 1 and 2 split that yes into affects learning and does not affect learning from 2015 onwards.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Physical disability","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC condition item with learning-effect codes","def":"A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes and affects learning (cycle 3 onwards), 2 yes but does not affect learning (cycle 3 onwards), 3 yes (cycles 1 and 2), 88 don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"Counting only code 1 produces a false break at 2015, because the same children were coded 3 in the two earlier cycles; any yes count has to add 1, 2 and 3. The column also names no condition and no severity, and the judgement that learning is affected is the classroom teacher's, not a clinical assessment.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D10","d":"The gate question for the child's other conditions: whether the child has any specific condition apart from a diagnosis that already qualifies them as special needs.","full":"The gate question for the child's other conditions: whether the child has any specific condition apart from a diagnosis that already qualifies them as special needs. The AEDC's purpose is \"To identify if the child has some other specific condition\", and beneath it sit the named flags D10AY through D10ZY, one per condition. It entered the instrument in the 2015 cycle and appears in the PLIDA 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024 special-needs tables.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Other specific condition","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC other specific condition gate item","def":"A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes, 88 don't know, the AvEDI's standard code for an item the teacher could not answer.","p":"2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It says nothing about how many conditions or which ones, and the named condition flags below it only reach PLIDA from the 2018 table, so for the 2015 cycle a 1 here cannot be resolved into anything. A 0 also does not rule out a qualifying diagnosis, which is what SPECIALNEEDS and the DIAGNOSIS series record.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":12},{"n":"D10A","d":"Whether the child has an enduring problem in the form of a chronic illness, asked on the instrument as \"Does the child have any (other) specific condition – Chronic illness (e.g. Otitis Media)\".","full":"Whether the child has an enduring problem in the form of a chronic illness, asked on the instrument as \"Does the child have any (other) specific condition – Chronic illness (e.g. Otitis Media)\". It is the oldest of three broad other-problem items, running from 2009, alongside D10B for neurodevelopmental disorder and D10C for anything else. From the 2018 tables the named flags D10AY to D10ZY cover much of the same ground far more finely, and the two generations of item overlap without any rule saying which to prefer.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10a","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Other enduring problems - Chronic Illness","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC other enduring problem item","def":"A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes, 88 don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10a","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It was not asked everywhere. The dictionary records it as \"Not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1/2\", so a national chronic illness count for 2009 or 2012 built from this column is short by the whole of New South Wales. The illness itself is not named, and the otitis media example printed on the instrument is likely to pull teachers towards ear infection.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":12},{"n":"D10AAY","d":"Whether the child has hydrocephalus, where hydrocephalus is not the diagnosis qualifying them as special needs.","full":"Whether the child has hydrocephalus, where hydrocephalus is not the diagnosis qualifying them as special needs. The PLIDA item list spells the condition 'Hydrodephalus', which is a typographical error: the AEDC element is hydrocephalus, and its purpose is \"To identify that the child has the condition 'Hydrocephalus' but it does not qualify the child as Special needs\". It was added to the instrument for the 2018 cycle, so it appears only in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 special-needs tables, with DIAGNOSIS27 recording the qualifying case.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10aay","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hydrodephalus","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC other specific condition flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes. The field is one character wide, so the AvEDI's standard missing codes, 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable, cannot be stored in it and an unanswered item is system missing instead.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10aay","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It says nothing about whether the condition is congenital or acquired, whether a shunt is in place, or whether the child needs support at school. Because the flag runs only where the condition did not qualify the child as special needs, this column on its own understates hydrocephalus and has to be read together with DIAGNOSIS27.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":2},{"n":"D10ABY","d":"Whether the child has muscular dystrophy, where it is not the diagnosis qualifying them as special needs.","full":"Whether the child has muscular dystrophy, where it is not the diagnosis qualifying them as special needs. The AEDC's purpose is \"To identify that the child has the condition 'Muscular Dystrophy' but it does not qualify the child as Special needs\". It was added for the 2018 cycle and appears in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 special-needs tables, with DIAGNOSIS29 carrying the qualifying case and D1 recording whether a physical disability affects the child's school work.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10aby","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Muscular dystrophy","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC other specific condition flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes. The field is one character wide, so the AvEDI's standard missing codes, 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable, cannot be stored in it and an unanswered item is system missing instead.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10aby","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It does not distinguish the forms of the disease or record the child's current mobility, so a child in an early and still-ambulant stage and a child already using a wheelchair carry the same 1. It is also a single point in a child's first school year, and the AEDC does not revisit the child, so progression cannot be observed.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":2},{"n":"D10ACY","d":"Whether the child has neurofibromatosis, where it is not the diagnosis qualifying them as special needs.","full":"Whether the child has neurofibromatosis, where it is not the diagnosis qualifying them as special needs. The AEDC's purpose is \"To identify that the child has the condition 'Neurofibromatosis' but it does not qualify the child as Special needs\". The AEDC's purpose for the element is \"To identify that the child has the condition 'Anaphylaxis' but it does not qualify the child as Special needs\", so the item is asked with a different preamble depending on SPECIALNEEDS and can never be the qualifying diagnosis itself; DIAGNOSIS1 on the same row records the qualifying case. It was added for the 2018 cycle and appears in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 special-needs tables, with DIAGNOSIS24 carrying the qualifying case.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10yy","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Does the child have any specific condition? cystic fibrosis","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC other specific condition flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes. The field is one character wide, so the AvEDI's standard missing codes, 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable, cannot be stored in it and an unanswered item is system missing instead.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10yy","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It gives no measure of lung function, daily treatment burden or school time lost, all of which vary widely between children carrying the same 1. It entered the instrument for the 2018 cycle, appears in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 special-needs tables, and DIAGNOSIS26 records the qualifying case.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10zy","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Fragile x","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC other specific condition flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes. The field is one character wide, so the AvEDI's standard missing codes, 88 for don't know and 99 for not applicable, cannot be stored in it and an unanswered item is system missing instead.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10zy","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It does not distinguish a fully affected child from a carrier, and it carries no measure of intellectual disability, so any learning effect has to come from the LANGCOG domain score or the special-needs flag rather than from this column. It is the teacher's own judgement rather than a diagnosis, and it closes the block of condition items D1 to D10 in the special-needs table. Like the D1 to D9 condition items, and unlike the D10 family, it is carried on both the complete and core AEDC files, and it runs in all six cycles from 2009, so it is the most consistently available signal of unmet need in the collection.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D11","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Needs further assessment","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC teacher assessment referral opinion","def":"A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes, 88 don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D11","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It is an opinion, not a referral. Nothing records whether an assessment followed, what kind was meant, or whether the child had already been assessed, and because the AEDC does not follow children up, a 1 cannot be linked to an outcome inside the collection. DEVDIFF on the same row is the derived summary of reported difficulties and answers a different question.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":12},{"n":"D2","d":"Whether the child has a visual impairment and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning.","full":"Whether the child has a visual impairment and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning. The AEDC's purpose is \"To identify if the child has a visual impairment that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom\". It sits with D1 physical disability and D3 hearing impairment as the sensory and physical items answered for every child, and from the 2015 tables DIAGNOSIS7 separately records blindness where that is the diagnosis qualifying the child as special needs.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D2","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Visual impairment","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC condition item with learning-effect codes","def":"A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes and affects learning (cycle 3 onwards), 2 yes but does not affect learning (cycle 3 onwards), 3 yes (cycles 1 and 2), 88 don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D2","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It cannot find undetected vision problems. Many children have their first eye test after starting school, so a child who cannot see the board but has never been assessed reads as 0, and the column also does not say whether an impairment is corrected by glasses already in use.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D3","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported a hearing impairment, one of the nine emerging-needs items D1 to D9 recorded for every child on the teacher instrument.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported a hearing impairment, one of the nine emerging-needs items D1 to D9 recorded for every child on the teacher instrument. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the field as a \"Variable to indicate if the child has a hearing impairment\" and prints the instrument text as \"Do any of the conditions/impairments below influence this student's ability to do school work in a regular classroom – hearing impairment\", the wording used in 2009 and 2012; the dictionary's appendix on the emerging-needs items records that in 2015 the question was broadened to ask \"Does the child have any of the following conditions / impairments / problems\", with separate answers for conditions that do and do not affect learning. It is the teacher's own judgement and needs no diagnosis, which separates it from DIAGNOSIS10 (deaf) in the same table, a diagnosis recorded only for children given special needs status.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D3","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hearing impairment","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC emerging needs item (teacher-reported condition affecting school work)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 \"Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 2 \"Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 3 \"Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)\" and 88 don't know. The split between codes 1 and 2 arrived with the 2015 instrument; before that any positive answer was code 3.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D3","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It does not measure hearing loss. From 2015 a child with a diagnosed loss the teacher judges not to hold back classroom work is coded 2, and the same child in 2009 or 2012 would have been coded 0 because the question then asked only about impairments affecting school work. Adding codes 1, 2 and 3 into one series across cycles therefore compares two different questions.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D4","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported a speech impairment they see in the classroom.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported a speech impairment they see in the classroom. The dictionary calls it a \"Variable to indicate if the child has a speech impairment\", asked as part of \"Does the child have any of the following conditions / impairments / problems? - speech impairment\", although the PLIDA data item list labels the column speech/language impairment. From 2015 the teacher chooses whether the impairment affects learning, and DEVDIFF in the same table counts only the answers that do.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D4","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Speech/language impairment","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC emerging needs item (teacher-reported condition affecting school work)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 \"Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 2 \"Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 3 \"Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)\" and 88 don't know. The split between codes 1 and 2 arrived with the 2015 instrument; before that any positive answer was code 3.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D4","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It is not a language assessment. The Language and Cognitive Skills domain score on the core table (LANGCOG and its four sub-scales) is a scored measure built from many items, while this is one teacher tick, and neither has anything to do with LANG, ESL or LBOTE on the core table, which record speaking a language other than English rather than an impairment.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D5","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported a learning disability affecting classroom work.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported a learning disability affecting classroom work. The dictionary defines the field as a \"Variable to indicate if the child has a learning disability\" and gives the purpose as identifying \"a learning disability that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom\". Because AEDC is collected in a child's first year of full-time school, this is usually a teacher's early impression rather than an assessed condition, and D11 beside it records whether the teacher thinks further assessment is needed.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D5","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Learning disability","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC emerging needs item (teacher-reported condition affecting school work)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 \"Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 2 \"Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 3 \"Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)\" and 88 don't know. A formal dyslexia or dyspraxia diagnosis at this age is rare and is recorded separately in DIAGNOSIS12 and DIAGNOSIS13, and only for children already flagged special needs, so the two columns will disagree by a wide margin for reasons that have nothing to do with the child.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D6","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported an emotional problem affecting classroom work.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported an emotional problem affecting classroom work. The dictionary describes it as a \"Variable to indicate if the child has an emotional problem\", one of the nine emerging-needs items the teacher completes for every child, and its purpose as identifying \"an emotional condition that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom\". It feeds DEVDIFF, but only when the teacher chose the answer that affects learning.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Emotional problem","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC emerging needs item (teacher-reported condition affecting school work)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 \"Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 2 \"Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 3 \"Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)\" and 88 don't know. EMOT and its four sub-scales on the core table are scored from the instrument and cut at the 2009 baseline percentiles, whereas this is a single yes-or-no. A child with special needs status has no EMOT category at all, so the two measures do not even cover the same children.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D7","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported a behavioural problem affecting classroom work.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported a behavioural problem affecting classroom work. The dictionary defines it as a \"Variable to indicate if the child has a behavioural problem\" and, from 2015, lets the teacher mark it as affecting learning or not. It records what the teacher observes in class, unlike DIAGNOSIS20 (oppositional defiant disorder) in the same table, which records a clinical diagnosis and only for children with special needs status.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D7","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Behavioural problem","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC emerging needs item (teacher-reported condition affecting school work)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 \"Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 2 \"Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 3 \"Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)\" and 88 don't know. The split between codes 1 and 2 arrived with the 2015 instrument; before that any positive answer was code 3.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D7","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"Dropping the 88 responses quietly turns them into no. Don't-know is a real code on this item, and a teacher who has had the child for only a few weeks is the most likely person to use it, so a naive 0-versus-not-0 recode understates behavioural problems most in exactly the classrooms with the least settled enrolment. TMSCH on the core table flags children in school less than one month.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D8","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported problems at home or in the home environment affecting the child's school work.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported problems at home or in the home environment affecting the child's school work. The dictionary defines it as a \"Variable to indicate if the child has problems at home\", which makes it the one item in the D1 to D9 block that is about the child's circumstances rather than a condition of the child. The teacher answers it from what they know of the family, with no definition of what counts as a problem.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D8","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Home environment/problems at home","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC emerging needs item (teacher-reported condition affecting school work)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 \"Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 2 \"Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)\", 3 \"Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)\" and 88 don't know. The split between codes 1 and 2 arrived with the 2015 instrument; before that any positive answer was code 3.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D8","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It is not a measure of family disadvantage. Nothing tells the teacher what to count, so the item picks up what a school happens to know, which varies with how much contact the family has had; the SEIFA score and category on the core table are the area-based measure and are built from Census data, not from the teacher. The PLIDA topic tag on this column, energy and environment, reads the word environment wrongly.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"D9","d":"Whether the child's teacher reported the child as affected by trauma, isolation or difficulties associated with resettlement.","full":"Whether the child's teacher reported the child as affected by trauma, isolation or difficulties associated with resettlement. The dictionary gives it as a \"Variable to indicate if the child is affected by trauma, isolation or difficulties associated with resettlement\", carried as one item on the instrument since 2009. The split between codes 1 and 2 arrived with the 2015 instrument; before that any positive answer was code 3.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D9","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It cannot tell you which of the three things happened. A child bereaved by a death, a child living far from other children and a newly arrived refugee child all produce the same code, so it cannot stand in for a refugee or humanitarian-entrant flag; COUNTRY, PLACEOFBIRTH and ARRIVALYEAR on the core table are what carry migration history.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":17},{"n":"DAYCARE","d":"Whether the child was reported as attending a day care centre in the year before starting school.","full":"Whether the child was reported as attending a day care centre in the year before starting school. The dictionary defines it as a \"Variable to indicate the child attended a day care centre\" and marks its source as derived, not asked: for 2009 and 2012 it is set when E2a, E2b or E2c was ticked, and from 2015 when E3ay is 1 to 3. It counts day care with and without a preschool programme, so DAYCARENO beside it is the subset without one, while PRESCHOOL and PSDC are the other two derived attendance flags built from the same questions.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item Daycare and Appendix 3 section A2.2.4","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Attended a day care centre","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC derived childcare attendance flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes, 88 don't know. The dictionary notes the derived childcare items are only based to have data when E2, whether the child was in any non-parental care or early childhood programme, was answered yes or no.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item Daycare and Appendix 3 section A2.2.4","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"A 0 is not evidence the child did not attend. The dictionary warns that these derived items are coded no when the answers behind them were don't know, and that a teacher who ticked day care at E2by but answered no or don't know at E3ay is coded as not having gone to day care. The teacher is also reporting second-hand on the year before school rather than from an enrolment record, so this is weaker evidence of attendance than a childcare administrative source.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":12},{"n":"DAYCARENO","d":"Whether the child attended a day care centre that did not run a preschool or kindergarten programme, in the year before starting school.","full":"Whether the child attended a day care centre that did not run a preschool or kindergarten programme, in the year before starting school. The dictionary defines it as a \"Variable to indicate the child attended day care without a pre-school program\" and derives it from E2b or E2c before 2015 and from E3ay together with E2y or E2by from 2015. Read against DAYCARE and PRESCHOOL in the same table it separates care from early education: a child with DAYCARENO of 1 and PRESCHOOL of 0 had childcare but no preschool programme in that year.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item Daycareno and Appendix 3 section A2.2.4","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Attended day care without pre-school program","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC derived childcare attendance flag","def":"A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes, 88 don't know, populated only where E2 was answered yes or no.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item Daycareno and Appendix 3 section A2.2.4","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It cannot be read as a count of children who missed out on preschool. The split depends on the teacher knowing whether the centre ran a preschool programme, and because a don't-know answer on any input variable is derived as no, an unsure teacher produces a 0 here rather than a 1. Only code 1 counts: from 2015 an answer of \"Yes - but does not affect learning\" leaves DEVDIFF at 0.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DevDiff and Appendix 3 section A2.2.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Having developmental difficulties","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC derived developmental difficulty flag","def":"A two-digit integer taking 0 or 1 only, with no don't-know or missing code, even though several of the D items it is built from do have an 88 code.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DevDiff and Appendix 3 section A2.2.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It undercounts the children a teacher actually flagged. It is also not the same thing as SPECIALNEEDS on the core table: a child can be DEVDIFF of 1 with no special needs status, and a child with special needs status can be DEVDIFF of 0.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":2},{"n":"DIAGNOSIS1","d":"Whether anaphylaxis was named as a diagnosis qualifying the child for special needs status.","full":"Whether anaphylaxis was named as a diagnosis qualifying the child for special needs status. Global developmental delay is often used as a working label before a specific diagnosis is reached, which makes it the diagnosis most likely to appear alongside others in the same row.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item Diagnosis19","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Global Developmental Delay","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC special needs qualifying diagnosis flag","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 no, 1 yes. The dictionary describes it as \"Vulnerable - One or more domains\" and notes that \"Vulnerability Summary Indicators do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on\", so it is derived from PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY beside it. Vulnerable means a domain category of 1, the 0 to 10th percentile band, cut against the 2009 baseline that is held fixed for every later cycle so that cycles can be compared.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1 and section 3.2 Summary Indicators","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Vulnerable - one or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC vulnerability summary indicator","def":"A one-digit integer taking 0 or 1.
