DV1 also says nothing about which domain or how far below the cut-off the child fell; LOWTOTAL and the five category columns carry that.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"DV1FLAG","d":"Whether the child belongs in the denominator when a developmentally-vulnerable-on-one-or-more rate is calculated.","full":"Whether the child belongs in the denominator when a developmentally-vulnerable-on-one-or-more rate is calculated. The dictionary defines it as \"Qualifies for the denominator of DV1\" and explains that the flag exists because, when the Canadian Early Development Instrument was adapted for Australia, \"work was conducted to refine the denominator (i.e., valid cases) for these two indicators to maximise the number of cases with reportable data\". A published AEDC rate is therefore the count of DV1 equal to 1 over the count of DV1FLAG equal to 1, not over every row in the file.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1Flag and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Qualifies for the denominator of dv1","k":"AEDC summary indicator denominator flag","def":"A one-digit integer taking 0 or 1, where 1 means the child's record supports a DV1 result.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1Flag and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf?sfvrsn=92bcf59b_1","lim":"It is not a quality flag for the record as a whole. It is built by counting how many of PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY equal 1, the 0 to 10th percentile band of the 2009 national baseline. The dictionary notes that summary indicators \"do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on\". DV2FLAG on the same row says whether the child counts in the denominator when the percentage is worked out.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.2 Summary Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Vulnerable - two or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC vulnerability summary indicator (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes. It is derived rather than collected, and the dictionary publishes no separate code for children who fall outside the DV2 denominator.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.2 Summary Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is not a count of vulnerable domains, so it cannot separate a child vulnerable on two domains from one vulnerable on all five; LOWTOTAL carries the count. A 0 also does not prove the child was assessed on all five domains, because children excluded from the denominator can read as 0, which is exactly why DV2FLAG exists.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"DV2FLAG","d":"Whether this child belongs in the denominator when the percentage developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains is calculated.","full":"Whether this child belongs in the denominator when the percentage developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains is calculated. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains\", which means a correct DV2 rate is the mean of DV2 over the rows where this flag is 1, not over all rows. It exists because children with a special needs diagnosis, children aged three and children with too few valid domain scores are excluded from AEDC vulnerability reporting.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Qualifies for the denominator of dv2","k":"AEDC denominator qualification flag (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes. Derived from the per-domain validity flags together with special needs status and age.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It says nothing about the child's development, so filtering on it selects a reporting population rather than a vulnerable one. It is also not interchangeable with the per-domain validity flags such as EMOTVALID: a child can hold a valid score on one domain and still fail to qualify for the DV2 denominator.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"E1","d":"The teacher's report of whether the child had attended an early intervention program before starting school, asked as \"To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended an early intervention program\".","full":"The teacher's report of whether the child had attended an early intervention program before starting school, asked as \"To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended an early intervention program\". In the special needs table it sits with D1 to D10, the enduring problem flags for physical, sensory, speech, learning, emotional and behavioural difficulties, and with D11 which asks whether the child needs further assessment, so it is the service-use column beside a set of need columns. It is the closest thing the AEDC holds to a record of a child having received support before school entry.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Attended an early intervention program","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC teacher-reported early intervention attendance (yes/no/don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer: 0 for no, 1 for yes and 88 for the standard AEDC don't-know code.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It names no program, no provider, no age at entry and no duration, so it cannot distinguish a single speech pathology block from three years of intensive support. Because the answer is the teacher's, 88 records only that the teacher did not know, and a 0 can mean the teacher was unaware rather than that no program was attended.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2009 / aedc_2009_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2012 / aedc_2012_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2015 / aedc_2015_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2018 / aedc_2018_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2021 / aedc_2021_spec","madipge-aedc-d-specialneeds-2024 / aedc_2024_spec"],"dom":12},{"n":"E2AY","d":"How many hours a week, on average, the child attended the preschool or kindergarten program reported in E2Y, banded around the fifteen-hour national benchmark.","full":"How many hours a week, on average, the child attended the preschool or kindergarten program reported in E2Y, banded around the fifteen-hour national benchmark. The dictionary states its purpose as \"To identify if the child was in regular educational programs for the mandatory amount of time\", so the three bands are less than fifteen hours, fifteen hours, and more than fifteen hours. It is only answered where E2Y records attendance, and E2BY on the same row says what kind of setting the program ran in.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2ay","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge did the child attend the preschool / kindergarten program on average:","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC preschool attendance intensity band","def":"A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for less than 15 hours per week, 2 for 15 hours per week, 3 for more than 15 hours per week, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2ay","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It records a weekly average, not how long the child stayed enrolled, so a child who attended fifteen hours a week for one term is indistinguishable from one who did so for the full year. The bands also carry no information about attendance actually taken up, only about the program the child was enrolled in.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":13},{"n":"E2BY","d":"What kind of service delivered the preschool or kindergarten program the child attended in the year before school, separating a standalone preschool or kindergarten from a long day care centre.","full":"What kind of service delivered the preschool or kindergarten program the child attended in the year before school, separating a standalone preschool or kindergarten from a long day care centre. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying \"the organisational basis for the child's preschool / kindergarten\", which is the distinction most Australian early childhood policy work needs, because the same entitlement is delivered through both service types. It is answered only where E2Y records attendance, and E2AY gives the hours.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"In what kind of setting was the preschool / kindergarten program?","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC preschool program setting type","def":"A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for preschool or kindergarten, 2 for long day care centre, 3 for other, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It identifies a setting type, not a provider, a funding source or a governance arrangement, so it cannot separate a government preschool from an independent or community one. Code 3 is an undifferentiated catch-all, so mobile, occasional care and school-attached services cannot be told apart from one another.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":13},{"n":"E2Y","d":"Whether the child attended a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher.","full":"Whether the child attended a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. It is the gate for the rest of the preschool block: E2AY records the weekly hours and E2BY the setting, and both are answered only where this column records attendance. The dictionary describes it as the variable that identifies \"if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school\", and it was introduced in 2018 in place of the earlier E2 series of childcare and preschool items.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge did the child attend a preschool / kindergarten program in the year before entering full-time school?","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC preschool attendance indicator (yes/no/don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer with three codes: 1 for yes, 2 for no, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in 2018.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"The coding is 1 for yes and 2 for no, unlike most AEDC yes/no items which use 0 and 1, so treating this as a 0/1 dummy turns every non-attender into an attender. It also does not carry back to earlier cycles: before 2018 the same information came from a different set of items, so an unadjusted trend from 2009 is not comparable.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":18},{"n":"E3AY","d":"Whether the child was in long day care on a regular basis in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time.","full":"Whether the child was in long day care on a regular basis in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the first of six parallel columns, E3AY to E3FY, that cover long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative, a nanny and any other person, each coded the same way. Version 8.0 of the dictionary corrected the instruction on all six, recording that they are \"asked to All\" rather than only to children whose E2Y records a preschool program.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child been in the following forms of non-parental care on a regular basis in the year before entering full time school: long day care","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC non-parental care intensity (long day care)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"No is coded 4, not 0, so a naive greater-than-zero test counts every non-attender as attending. Long day care here also overlaps with E2Y, because a long day care centre can deliver the preschool program reported there, so adding the E3 columns and E2Y together double counts the same child.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"E3BY","d":"Whether the child was regularly in family day care in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time.","full":"Whether the child was regularly in family day care in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. Family day care is the regulated home-based service, so this column separates it from the centre-based care in E3AY and from the informal relative care in E3CY and E3DY. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying \"how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school\", and the 2018 cycle rebuilt it from the earlier E2e and E2etime pair.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child been in the following forms of non-parental care on a regular basis in the year before entering full time school: family day care","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC non-parental care intensity (family day care)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"The full-time and part-time split is the only intensity information available, so it cannot yield hours, days per week or weeks of the year. Code 3 is a real answer rather than a missing value, and dropping it as missing biases any full-time share upwards.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"E3CY","d":"Whether a grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time.","full":"Whether a grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. This is the largest of the informal care categories in Australia and the reason the E3 block distinguishes grandparents from other relatives, who are captured separately in E3DY. Because the columns are a multiple response set, a child can be recorded here and in the formal care columns E3AY and E3BY at the same time.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child been in the following forms of non-parental care on a regular basis in the year before entering full time school: grandparent","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC non-parental care intensity (grandparent)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It does not say whether the grandparent lived with the child, was paid, or was the child's primary carer, so it cannot identify kinship care arrangements or grandparent-headed households. The teacher is answering about a household arrangement they did not observe, so the don't-know rate is a property of teacher knowledge rather than of the family.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"E3DY","d":"Whether a relative other than a parent or grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time.","full":"Whether a relative other than a parent or grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the residual family category in the E3 block: grandparents are taken out into E3CY, and unrelated carers fall to E3EY for a nanny or E3FY for a friend or neighbour. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying \"if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school\".","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child been in the following forms of non-parental care on a regular basis in the year before entering full time school: other relative","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC non-parental care intensity (other relative)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"The relationship itself is not recorded, so an aunt, an adult sibling and a cousin all collapse into one code and no family structure can be reconstructed from it. It also cannot be read as a measure of family support, since a family with no relative nearby and a family that declined help both record 4.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"E3EY","d":"Whether a nanny regularly cared for the child in the home in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time.","full":"Whether a nanny regularly cared for the child in the home in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the paid, unregulated, in-home category of the E3 block, distinct from the regulated home-based service captured in E3BY as family day care. Version 7.0 of the dictionary lists a correction to the field format and field values across E3ay to E3fy, so the published code list for this column is not identical in earlier dictionary releases.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child been in the following forms of non-parental care on a regular basis in the year before entering full time school: nanny","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC non-parental care intensity (nanny)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It does not distinguish a live-in nanny from one who visits, or paid work from a reciprocal arrangement, so it cannot support any inference about household income. It is also a narrow category, so any subgroup estimate built on it should be checked against the AEDC suppression rules before it is reported.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"E3FY","d":"Whether someone outside the family, such as a friend or a neighbour, regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time.","full":"Whether someone outside the family, such as a friend or a neighbour, regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It closes the E3 block as the catch-all: anything that was not long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative or a nanny lands here. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying care \"with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school\".","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child been in the following forms of non-parental care on a regular basis in the year before entering full time school: other (includes friend or neighbour)","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC non-parental care intensity (other person)","def":"A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"Being the residual category, it holds arrangements with nothing in common beyond not fitting the five named ones, so a positive value supports no statement about the type or quality of care. It is also the category a teacher is least likely to know about, so a low count here reflects reporting as much as behaviour.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"E4","d":"Whether the child attended a playgroup at any point in the years before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher.","full":"Whether the child attended a playgroup at any point in the years before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. Its reference window is deliberately wider than the rest of the E block: E2Y and the E3 columns ask about the single year before school, while this one asks about \"the years before entering full time school\". The dictionary records that it was introduced in the 2012 cycle and renamed from E3b in 2015, so its name in older AEDC extracts is not E4.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"To the best of your knowledge has this child attended playgroup in the years before entering full time school","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC playgroup attendance indicator (yes/no/don't know)","def":"A two-digit integer with three codes: 0 for no, 1 for yes, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It records attendance ever, not how often or for how long, so a single visit and three years of weekly sessions are the same value. It also does not identify the type of playgroup, so supported and intensive playgroups aimed at families with additional needs cannot be separated from ordinary community ones.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":12},{"n":"E5","d":"The teacher's rating of how well the child is settling into school, asked as whether the child \"is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school\".","full":"The teacher's rating of how well the child is settling into school, asked as whether the child \"is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school\". It is one of three closing instrument questions, with E6 on parental engagement and E7 on reading at home, all sharing the same three-point scale. None of the three feed the five AEDC domain scores, so this column is an independent read on school transition rather than a component of the developmental measures.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is adapting to school","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)","def":"A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is one teacher's global impression at a single point in the child's first school year, not a validated scale, so it cannot be treated as an outcome measure comparable to a domain score. The three points are ordinal and unequally spaced, so averaging them across a school or community produces a number with no defined unit.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":1},{"n":"E6","d":"The teacher's rating of whether the child's parents or caregivers are actively engaged with the school in supporting the child's learning.","full":"The teacher's rating of whether the child's parents or caregivers are actively engaged with the school in supporting the child's learning. It is the school-side view of family involvement, and it pairs with E7, which asks about reading at home, to give two crude proxies for the home learning environment. The dictionary records that it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, a filter that was only lifted in 2015.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Parents actively engaged with the school","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)","def":"A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"New South Wales children are missing for the first two cycles, so a national trend that ignores this treats a coverage change as a real change in parental engagement. The rating also measures engagement visible to the school, so families who support learning at home without contacting the school score low on something they are doing.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":1},{"n":"E7","d":"The teacher's rating of whether the child is regularly read to, or encouraged in reading, at home.","full":"The teacher's rating of whether the child is regularly read to, or encouraged in reading, at home. The question wording ends \"as far as you can tell\", which flags on the instrument itself that the teacher is inferring a home behaviour rather than observing it. Like E6, it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, and the same three-point scale is used for both.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is regularly read to at home","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)","def":"A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is a teacher's inference about the household, so it will partly track how much contact the family has with the school rather than what happens at home. Reading in a language other than English is not asked about separately, so a home rich in reading in another language can be rated as not true.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":1},{"n":"EMOT","d":"The child's score on emotional maturity, one of the five AEDC developmental domains, built from the teacher's answers to the emotional maturity items on the instrument.","full":"The child's score on emotional maturity, one of the five AEDC developmental domains, built from the teacher's answers to the emotional maturity items on the instrument. The dictionary states that for each domain \"children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development\", and that a score is only produced where at least 75 per cent of the domain's items were completed. EMOT_1 to EMOT_4 on the same row break it into prosocial and helping behaviour, anxious and fearful behaviour, aggressive behaviour, and hyperactive and inattentive behaviour, while EMOTCATEGORY converts the score into the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Emotional maturity","k":"AEDC domain score, zero to ten","def":"A continuous numeric value from 0 to 10, stored with four decimal places. The bands are 0 to 10th, 11th to 25th, 26th to 50th and 51st to 100th percentile, so band 1 is vulnerable, band 2 is at risk and bands 3 and 4 are on track. The cut-offs are fixed against the 2009 national collection: the dictionary states they \"have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared\".","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Vulnerable - emotional maturity","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain percentile category (four bands)","def":"A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th. The percentile positions are those of the 2009 baseline distribution, adjusted for age variation across children in their first year of school.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"The bands do not describe the current cohort, so a 12 per cent vulnerable rate in 2021 means 12 per cent scored below the 2009 tenth percentile, not that 12 per cent were in the bottom decile of 2021. The dictionary also states that domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs or aged under four, so their category is absent rather than high.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":0},{"n":"EMOTVALID","d":"Whether the child's emotional maturity result counts as valid for AEDC reporting.","full":"Whether the child's emotional maturity result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. The dictionary defines a 1 as \"Child does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain\", so a single flag folds three separate exclusions together. There is one of these per domain, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of the five a child is valid on.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Valid - emotional maturity","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain validity flag (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for this domain; 1 otherwise.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"A 0 does not tell you which of the three reasons applied, so it cannot be used to identify children with special needs or to measure teacher non-response. It is also domain specific, so a child can be valid on physical health and invalid on emotional maturity, and dropping every row with any invalid flag discards usable results on the other domains.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"ESL","d":"Whether the teacher considers the child to have English as a second language, asked on the instrument as \"Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)\".","full":"Whether the teacher considers the child to have English as a second language, asked on the instrument as \"Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)\". It is one of three overlapping language columns and the most subjective: LANG asks whether a language other than English is spoken at home, and LBOTE is derived rather than asked. B1, the rating of the child's ability to use English effectively, sits alongside it and is the closer measure of proficiency.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"ESL (english as a second language)","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC English as a second language indicator (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is a teacher's classification, not a test, and it carries no threshold, so it varies with how each jurisdiction and school uses the label. A child can be ESL with fluent conversational English, and an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander child speaking Aboriginal English or Kriol may or may not be flagged depending on local practice, so an ESL rate cannot be read as an English proficiency rate.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"GCCSACODE","d":"GCCSA code","vp":"official","od":"GCCSA code","k":"asgs2021_gccsa_code","def":"The source publishes this value domain.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables (accompanying workbook), Australian Government Department of Education, Table 3.1 ASGS - Main Structure","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables.xlsx?sfvrsn=75ae30bf_1","lim":"The source defines the value domain. The dictionary describes the data element as \"The sex of the child\" while giving its purpose as identifying the child's gender, which reflects a change made in 2024 when the instrument item was relabelled from sex to gender and expanded beyond a binary. Codes 1 for male and 2 for female carry every cycle, so which codes can occur depends on the collection year of the row.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sex of child","k":"AEDC child sex or gender code","def":"A one-digit integer. It is one of three nested Indigenous geographies on the row: ILOCCODE gives the Indigenous Location, IARECODE the Indigenous Area, and this column the Region that contains them both. It was introduced in the 2015 cycle, and IREGPUBLIC beside it says whether AEDC results for the region can be published.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography; codes in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous region code","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS Indigenous Region code","def":"A three-digit integer. The dictionary does not print the codes; they are published separately in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, which follow the ABS Indigenous Structure of the ASGS edition in force for the cycle.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography; codes in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is a geography of residence, so it describes where the child lives and says nothing about whether the child is Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander; ATSI is the column that does that. Indigenous Regions are also very large, with only a few dozen covering the country, so they cannot support any local analysis.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":24},{"n":"IREGNAME","d":"The written name of the ABS Indigenous Region that IREGCODE identifies, carried on the row so that output is readable without a lookup.","full":"The written name of the ABS Indigenous Region that IREGCODE identifies, carried on the row so that output is readable without a lookup. It is a label only, and the code beside it is what the ABS classification is built on. Names such as Alice Springs, Dubbo and Cape York are region labels, not the names of communities or of the AEDC local communities held in LOCALCOMMUNITY.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography; names in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous region name","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS Indigenous Region name","def":"Left-justified text up to 50 characters, taking its values from the Indigenous Region names published in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables for the relevant ASGS edition.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography; names in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"Region names are reused and occasionally revised between ASGS editions, so joining AEDC cycles on the name rather than on the code will silently mismatch regions whose boundary or label changed. A name also shares wording with towns and with AEDC communities, so string matching across geography levels produces false joins.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":25},{"n":"IREGPUBLIC","d":"Whether AEDC results for this child's Indigenous Region are publishable, and if not, which rule blocked them.","full":"Whether AEDC results for this child's Indigenous Region are publishable, and if not, which rule blocked them. The codes separate three distinct failures: fewer than fifteen valid AEDC children, fewer than two teachers, and the coverage rule that at least 80 per cent of non-special-needs children in the area were assessed. It is the same six-code scheme used by LGAPUBLIC, IAREPUBLIC, ILOCPUBLIC and the SA2 and SA3 equivalents, so one reading of the codes serves the whole family.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous region publishable","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC geographic reportability indicator","def":"An integer with six codes: 1 for results publicly available; 5 for less than 80 per cent of all non-special needs children; 9 for location not available; 21 for fewer than 15 valid AEDC children; 22 for fewer than two teachers; and 23 for both 21 and 22. The dictionary records a field length of 1 even though the suppression codes run to two digits.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It governs public reporting of the area, not the record in front of you, so a child in a region coded 21 still carries full domain scores in the microdata. Code 9 is a different problem from the rest: it says the child's location could not be resolved to a region at all, so filtering it out removes children with missing geography rather than children in small areas.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":26},{"n":"JCAMPUSID","d":"The campus code the state or territory education authority uses for the campus the child was assessed at.","full":"The campus code the state or territory education authority uses for the campus the child was assessed at. The dictionary defines it as \"The individual campus code used by the jurisdiction to identify each school campus participating in the AEDC\" and states that it is unique within jurisdiction and year. LOCATIONAGEID on the same row is the Australian Government's code for the same campus, and SCHOOLID is the school the campus belongs to.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 8 Pre-Instrument Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Jurisdictional campus identifier","k":"AEDC jurisdiction campus identifier","def":"A five-digit integer allocated by the jurisdiction. Uniqueness holds only within one jurisdiction and one collection year.","p":"2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 8 Pre-Instrument Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is not a national key and not stable over time, so the same value in two states is two different campuses and the same campus can change value between cycles. It is also suppressed for schools outside a data recipient's jurisdiction, so it is systematically blank rather than missing at random.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"LANG","d":"Whether the child speaks a language other than English at home, asked on the instrument as \"Does the child speak a language other than English at home\".","full":"Whether the child speaks a language other than English at home, asked on the instrument as \"Does the child speak a language other than English at home\". It is the gate for the whole language block: LANGUAGEID, ILANGUAGEID, CANCOM and the LANGSOURCE columns all carry the instruction \"Only answer if Lang = Yes\", so a blank in those columns means the question was never put rather than that the child speaks only English. ESL and LBOTE are the two related flags, and neither is the same measure.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Speaks language other than english","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC language other than English at home indicator (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It records home use, not proficiency in either language, so it cannot distinguish a child fluent in two languages from one with little English; CANCOM and B1 answer that. Because it filters the rest of the language block, treating a blank LANGUAGEID as English-speaking silently converts a skip into an observation.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"LANGCOG","d":"The child's score on the language and cognitive skills domain, which the AEDC qualifies as school-based because the items ask what the teacher observes the child doing in the classroom.","full":"The child's score on the language and cognitive skills domain, which the AEDC qualifies as school-based because the items ask what the teacher observes the child doing in the classroom. LANGCOG_1 to LANGCOG_4 on the same row split it into basic literacy, interest in literacy and numeracy and memory, advanced literacy, and basic numeracy. Like the other four domains it runs from zero to ten with higher scores meaning stronger development, and LANGCOGCATEGORY turns it into the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Language and cognitive skills","k":"AEDC domain score, zero to ten","def":"A continuous numeric value from 0 to 10, stored with four decimal places, formed from the domain's instrument items where at least 75 per cent of them were completed.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is measured through classroom English, so a child with strong literacy and numeracy in another language can score low on skills they hold; the domain is not a test administered to the child. The dictionary notes that the cut-offs \"take into account the age variations in the population of children in their first year of schooling\", so the bands are age adjusted rather than raw score thresholds.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Vulnerable - language and cognition","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain percentile category (four bands)","def":"A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th, all positioned against the 2009 national baseline.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"Because the boundaries are age adjusted and anchored to 2009, two children with the same LANGCOG score can sit in different bands, so the category cannot be reconstructed by ranking the score column. Children with a special needs diagnosis and children aged three receive no category, so their rows are blank rather than in band 4.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":0},{"n":"LANGCOGVALID","d":"Whether the child's language and cognitive skills result counts as valid for AEDC reporting.","full":"Whether the child's language and cognitive skills result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. A 0 means the child has special needs status, is three years old, or left too many of this domain's instrument questions unanswered; a 1 means none of those applied. It is the language and cognition member of a set of five, one per domain, and VALIDINSTRUMENT separately identifies children with fewer than four valid domain scores for the 80 per cent coverage rule.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Valid - language and cognitive skills","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain validity flag (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the domain result is not valid, 1 where it is. Because the same 0 covers special needs status, it is not safe to use this column as a proxy for teacher non-response on the language items.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"LANGSOURCE0","d":"Whether the teacher relied on a written record, meaning an enrolment form, an assessment or a report, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language.","full":"Whether the teacher relied on a written record, meaning an enrolment form, an assessment or a report, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the documentary option in a six-way multiple response set, LANGSOURCE0 to LANGSOURCE5, that records where the teacher's answer came from. The whole set is answered only where LANG records a language other than English at home.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Enrolment form, assessment, report or school survey","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)","def":"A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. It also documents the evidence behind CANCOM only, so it says nothing about how LANGUAGEID was determined or how the domain scores were formed.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-language-2009 / aedc_2009_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2012 / aedc_2012_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2015 / aedc_2015_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2018 / aedc_2018_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2021 / aedc_2021_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2024 / aedc_2024_lan"],"dom":27},{"n":"LANGSOURCE1","d":"Whether the teacher asked a parent, guardian, relative or friend of the child when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language.","full":"Whether the teacher asked a parent, guardian, relative or friend of the child when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the family-report option in the LANGSOURCE set, and the one that carries most weight for a child whose language the school has no records on. Selecting it does not exclude the other five options, since the underlying instrument question is select all that apply.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Parent, guardian, relative or friend","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)","def":"A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. Because the six columns are not mutually exclusive, they do not sum to one and cannot be collapsed into a single categorical source variable.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-language-2009 / aedc_2009_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2012 / aedc_2012_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2015 / aedc_2015_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2018 / aedc_2018_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2021 / aedc_2021_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2024 / aedc_2024_lan"],"dom":27},{"n":"LANGSOURCE2","d":"Whether the teacher relied on their own observation of the child, or on knowing the child, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language.","full":"Whether the teacher relied on their own observation of the child, or on knowing the child, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the only option in the LANGSOURCE set that involves no third party, so it marks answers based purely on classroom judgement. In practice a teacher who does not speak the home language is judging communication in a language they cannot assess.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Own observation or knowing child","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)","def":"A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. Only 2 means the source was used.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It carries no measure of how well the teacher knows the child or the language, so it cannot be used to grade the reliability of the CANCOM answer, only to note that no external source was consulted. It also does not indicate that the teacher observed the child speaking the language, merely that the teacher's own knowledge was the basis for the answer.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-language-2009 / aedc_2009_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2012 / aedc_2012_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2015 / aedc_2015_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2018 / aedc_2018_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2021 / aedc_2021_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2024 / aedc_2024_lan"],"dom":27},{"n":"LANGSOURCE3","d":"Whether the teacher consulted another staff member when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language.","full":"Whether the teacher consulted another staff member when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It sits between the family-report and documentary options in the LANGSOURCE set, and typically stands for a bilingual aide, a support teacher or a colleague who knows the family. LANGSOURCE5, held in the Indigenous table, is the parallel option for an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Other staff member","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)","def":"A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. It also overlaps in practice with LANGSOURCE5, so counting the two together will double count consultations with a staff member who is also the cultural consultant.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-language-2009 / aedc_2009_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2012 / aedc_2012_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2015 / aedc_2015_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2018 / aedc_2018_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2021 / aedc_2021_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2024 / aedc_2024_lan"],"dom":27},{"n":"LANGSOURCE4","d":"Whether the teacher used a source outside the named options when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language.","full":"Whether the teacher used a source outside the named options when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the residual member of the LANGSOURCE set, selected when the basis was neither a written record, a family member, the teacher's own knowledge, another staff member nor a cultural consultant. A high rate on this column is a signal that the named options do not cover how schools actually reach the answer.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Other sources","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)","def":"A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. It cannot be treated as a missing value indicator either, because it is a deliberate selection rather than a failure to answer.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-language-2009 / aedc_2009_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2012 / aedc_2012_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2015 / aedc_2015_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2018 / aedc_2018_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2021 / aedc_2021_lan","madipge-aedc-d-language-2024 / aedc_2024_lan"],"dom":27},{"n":"LANGSOURCE5","d":"Whether an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant was a source for the teacher's CANCOM answer about the child's ability to communicate in the home language.","full":"Whether an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant was a source for the teacher's CANCOM answer about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It sits in the Indigenous table beside ILANGUAGEID and the traditional language columns, because the consultant is the person best placed to judge communication in Aboriginal English, Kriol or a traditional language. The dictionary records that it was introduced in the 2015 cycle, so it does not exist for 2009 or 2012.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)","def":"A one-digit integer with three codes: 0 for unselected, 1 for no and 2 for yes. It is the third and broadest of the AEDC language flags, and the dictionary prints the rule that builds it: \"Children are considered 'LBOTE' if they speak a language other than English at home, or if they speak English at home but are still considered to have ESL (English as a second language) status.\" It is therefore the union of LANG and ESL, which is why it is always at least as large as either one on its own. The dictionary lists it among the variables whose names, descriptions or notes were corrected in the 2024 revision, so its published definition is not identical across dictionary versions.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"LBOTE indicator","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC language background other than English indicator (yes/no)","def":"A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes, with the source given as derived rather than instrument. It was introduced in the 2012 cycle, and LGAPUBLIC on the same row says whether AEDC results for that LGA are publishable.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"LGA code","t":"categorical","k":"ABS local government area code (child based)","def":"A five-digit integer on the ABS local government area classification, with the code list published in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables for the ASGS edition in force in the cycle.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It is not present for the 2009 cycle, since the column began in 2012, so a panel across all cycles has a structural gap rather than missing values. ABS reissues local government area codes annually, so the same council can carry different codes in different cycles and a code alone is not interpretable without the collection year.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":31},{"n":"LGANAME","d":"The written name of the local government area the child lives in, the label attached to LGACODE.","full":"The written name of the local government area the child lives in, the label attached to LGACODE. It is a thirty-character field, which is shorter than the forty characters used for the local community equivalent LCLGANAME, so longer council names can appear cut differently in the two columns. Like the code, it starts in the 2012 cycle.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"LGA name","t":"categorical","k":"ABS local government area name (child based)","def":"Left-justified text up to 30 characters, taking ABS local government area names from the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables for the edition in force in the cycle.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"Thirty characters is short enough to truncate long council names, so the text is not always a complete name and is unsafe as a display label without checking. Names are also not unique nationally, so grouping by this column alone merges same-named councils in different states.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":32},{"n":"LGAPUBLIC","d":"Whether AEDC results for the child's local government area can be published, and which rule blocked them if not.","full":"Whether AEDC results for the child's local government area can be published, and which rule blocked them if not. Code 1 means results are publicly available; codes 21, 22 and 23 mark small counts, fewer than two teachers, or both; code 5 marks a failure of the 80 per cent coverage rule; and code 9 means the location itself could not be determined. It uses the same six-code scheme as IREGPUBLIC, IAREPUBLIC, ILOCPUBLIC and the SA2 and SA3 publishability columns.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"LGA publishable","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC geographic reportability indicator","def":"An integer with six codes: 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 and 23, where 1 is publishable and the others each name a reason the area's results are withheld from public reporting. The dictionary records a field length of 1 even though the suppression codes run to two digits.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It constrains public reporting of the area, not access to the record, so children in an area coded 22 still carry full domain scores in the microdata and can be analysed. Reading anything other than 1 as missing data conflates a genuinely missing geography, code 9, with areas whose data exists but is too thin to publish.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":26},{"n":"LOCALCOMMUNITY","d":"Local community","vp":"ai","od":"Local community","k":"aedc_localcommunity_name","def":"The source publishes this value domain of 4,710 values.
