It is the key for the whole local community block on the row: LOCALCOMMUNITY holds the name, LCLGACODE the associated council, LCABSSEIFASCORE the area disadvantage score, and LCPUBLIC whether the community's results can be published. The boundaries are drawn to align with ABS Statistical Area Level 1 building blocks so that AEDC results can be compared with Census data.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography and section 4.1 Changes to the AEDC geography","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Local community identifier","k":"AEDC Local Community identifier","def":"A six-digit derived integer, with the code list published in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography and section 4.1 Changes to the AEDC geography","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"The identifier is not stable in meaning across releases: new local community boundaries were created in 2015 to align with the ASGS, and revised boundaries were introduced for the 2024 collection and applied retrospectively to all earlier cycles, so the same community can cover a different area than it did in an earlier extract. It was introduced in the 2021 collection to replace AGCampusID, and both were in use during that cycle before AGCampusID was discontinued in 2024. It is the national counterpart to JCAMPUSID, which is the jurisdiction's own code for the same campus.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 8 Pre-Instrument Variables","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"National campus identifier used by deewr","k":"AEDC Australian Government campus identifier","def":"A five-digit integer allocated nationally by the Australian Government. Introduced in the 2021 cycle and renamed from AGLocationID in 2024.","p":"2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 8 Pre-Instrument Variables","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionaryd96e1bdf-615e-47eb-bbf2-28d2be1f656b.pdf?sfvrsn=eb7383cd_1","lim":"It identifies a campus, not a school, so a multi-campus school has several values and counting distinct values here overstates the number of schools; SCHOOLID is the school-level key. Because it starts in 2021 and overlapped with AGCampusID in that cycle, a campus panel built on this column alone loses every earlier cycle and can double count 2021 campuses carrying both identifiers.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"LOWTOTAL","d":"A count, from zero to five, of the developmental domains on which the child scored in the bottom tenth of the 2009 national distribution.","full":"A count, from zero to five, of the developmental domains on which the child scored in the bottom tenth of the 2009 national distribution. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify the number of domains in which the child is in the 0 to 10th percentile category\", so it is the number of the five category columns - PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY - that equal 1. HIGHTOTAL is its mirror at the other end of the distribution, and the published summary indicators DV1 and DV2 are yes/no readings of this same count.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'LowTotal'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of domains in which child is vulnerable","k":"Count of AEDC domains in the vulnerable band (0 to 5)","def":"A single-digit integer from 0 to 5. The cut-off for each domain is the tenth percentile of the 2009 AEDC population and has been held fixed at that baseline for every cycle since, so the count is measured against 2009 children rather than against the child's own cohort.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'LowTotal'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It does not say which domains, so two children both counted at two can be vulnerable on entirely different pairs and only the five category columns separate them. A domain that could not be scored is simply not counted, which means a low value can mean strong development or missing information; VALIDDOMAINS and TOTALMISS are what tell those apart.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"MOC","d":"The calendar month in which the teacher completed the child's Australian version of the Early Development Instrument.","full":"The calendar month in which the teacher completed the child's Australian version of the Early Development Instrument. Collection runs in the first half of the school year, so the dictionary allows only five values, April through August, and the field is a single digit rather than a date. With YEAR it dates the assessment, and it is half of the age calculation: the dictionary says AEDC age \"is based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher\".","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'MOC' and section 4.4","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Month instrument completed","t":"categorical","k":"Month of AvEDI completion (April to August)","def":"A single-digit integer: 4 April, 5 May, 6 June, 7 July, 8 August. There is no day component and no value outside that window.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'MOC' and section 4.4","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It cannot order two assessments inside the same month, and it is not an enrolment date or a data-supply date. It is also not a neutral stamp: the dictionary says the domain cut-offs take account of age variation among children in their first year of school, but says nothing about time already spent at school, so an April child and an August child can differ on months of schooling in a way the published method does not address.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":34},{"n":"MSI","d":"Multiple strengths indicator score","vp":"ai","od":"Multiple strengths indicator score","k":"aedc_msi_score_0_39 (numeric, 0 to 39; count of MSI items on which the child shows a strength)","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Guidelines 2025, Australian Government Department of Education, section 2.1.3 Supplementary Indicators","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/aedc-data-guidelines.pdf?sfvrsn=12f779cf_1","lim":"The source defines the value domain but it is not listed here. Frequency information is not included.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":36},{"n":"ONTRACK0","d":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on none of the five AEDC domains, held only for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles.","full":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on none of the five AEDC domains, held only for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles. It is the one member of the legacy ONTRACK series with no modern successor: the dictionary records that ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 were rebuilt to the OT5 method and reissued as OT1 to OT4, but that \"OnTrack on no domains (OnTrack0) was not updated to the new methodology\". A six-cycle series of children on track nowhere therefore has to be built from the five domain category columns instead.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack0' and section 6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"On track on no domains","t":"categorical","k":"Legacy on-track summary flag (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns rather than reported by a teacher.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack0' and section 6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It carries no denominator flag of the kind OT1FLAG to OT5FLAG provide, so children whose domains could not be scored sit in the same value as children who were assessed and fell short everywhere. It is also not the complement of a published AEDC figure: the dictionary names only DV1, DV2 and OT5 as summary indicators, and an on-track-on-no-domains rate is not among them.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"ONTRACK1","d":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on at least one of the five domains, present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables only.","full":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on at least one of the five domains, present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables only. It is the superseded form of OT1: the dictionary records that ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 \"have been recalculated to align with the methodology for calculating OT5\", which produced OT1 to OT4 and a denominator flag for each. That is why the old and new names never appear in the same cycle table.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack1' and section 6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"On track on one or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"Legacy on-track summary flag (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack1' and section 6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Stacking this column for 2009 to 2015 onto OT1 for 2018 to 2024 creates a break that looks like a change in children: OT1 is reported over the OT1FLAG denominator and this column has no denominator rule at all. Being on track on one domain also says nothing about the other four, so it can be 1 for a child LOWTOTAL shows as vulnerable on three.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"ONTRACK2","d":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, carried in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables.","full":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, carried in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables. The dictionary describes it as \"On track on two or more domains\" and lists it as a Master unit record file variable introduced in 2009, before the AEDC had settled on a single strengths measure. From 2018 the equivalent is OT2, calculated on the aligned method and reported over the OT2FLAG denominator.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack2' and section 6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"On track on two or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"Legacy on-track summary flag (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived by counting the domains whose category column places the child above the 25th percentile.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack2' and section 6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"No AEDC national report publishes a two-or-more on-track rate, so a figure taken from this column has nothing published to check it against. It is also not the opposite of DV2, vulnerable on two or more domains: a child can be on track on two domains and vulnerable on two others, so both columns can read 1 for the same child.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"ONTRACK3","d":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, held for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles.","full":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, held for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify if the child is developmentally on track on three or more domains\", and its cumulative thresholds mean it is implied by ONTRACK4 and ONTRACK5 on the same row. OT3 is the 2018-onward replacement, built on the aligned method.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack3' and section 6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"On track on three or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"Legacy on-track summary flag (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no. The ONTRACK series is cumulative, so a child flagged here is also flagged on ONTRACK1 and ONTRACK2.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack3' and section 6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"The gap between this column and ONTRACK4 is the share on track on exactly three domains only because the legacy series shares one unrestricted denominator; the same subtraction on OT3 and OT4 is not safe, because those carry separate qualification flags. Three of five is also not a milestone the AEDC defines - the cut-offs are per domain, so the count has no interpretation beyond arithmetic.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"ONTRACK4","d":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables.","full":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify if the child is developmentally on track on four or more domains\", one step below the all-five threshold that became the AEDC's national strengths indicator. It was recalculated into OT4 for the 2024 collection and the PLIDA files carry OT4 from 2018 onward in its place.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack4' and section 6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"On track on four or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"Legacy on-track summary flag (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack4' and section 6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It is not the complement of DV1: a child on track on four domains and vulnerable on the fifth reads 1 here and 1 on DV1 at the same time, so the two cannot be used as opposite ends of one scale. Nor is it a near-miss version of ONTRACK5, since the domain a child falls short on is not recorded here and only the category columns show it.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"ONTRACK5","d":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on all five domains, on the calculation used up to the 2015 cycle.","full":"A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on all five domains, on the calculation used up to the 2015 cycle. This is the measure the Productivity Commission adopted in 2018 for the Closing the Gap target on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children thriving in their early years, which is why it was singled out for rebuilding: the dictionary records a decision \"to re-calculate the On Track on 5 domains (OnTrack5) to align with the Vulnerability Summary Indicators (DV1 and DV2)\" made in 2021, producing OT5 and OT5FLAG. In PLIDA this column covers 2009 to 2015 and the new pair covers 2018 to 2024.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack5' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"On track on five domains","t":"categorical","k":"Legacy on-track summary flag (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no. Like the other summary indicators it has no score and no cut-off of its own, resting on the five domain category columns.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack5' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Figures built from this column do not reproduce the 2021 National Report or the Closing the Gap tracking, which use OT5 over the OT5FLAG denominator; the dictionary is explicit that the new variables \"need to be used to replicate the figures\". Treating the old and new columns as one continuous series therefore puts an artificial step at the 2018 boundary.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"OT1","d":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on one or more of the five domains, calculated on the same basis as the vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2.","full":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on one or more of the five domains, calculated on the same basis as the vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2. The dictionary defines it as \"On Track - On one or more domain\" and records it as introduced for the 2024 collection, when the legacy ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 columns were recalculated; PLIDA carries it from the 2018 cycle, so the rebuilt series has been applied back across the earlier files. A rate from this column has to be taken over children with OT1FLAG equal to 1.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1' and section 6","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is developmentally on track on one or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC on-track summary indicator (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. It is derived from the five domain category columns; the summary indicators carry no score and no cut-off of their own.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1' and section 6","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"One or more domains on track is a very low bar and is not the AEDC's headline strengths measure, which is OT5 across all five. Reading a high rate here as good news inverts the intent, because the indicator is passed by a child who is developmentally vulnerable on the other four domains.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"OT1FLAG","d":"Marks whether the child counts in the denominator when an on-track-on-one-or-more rate is worked out.","full":"Marks whether the child counts in the denominator when an on-track-on-one-or-more rate is worked out. The dictionary defines it as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT1\" and its purpose as identifying whether the child qualifies for that calculation; AEDC summary indicators are published as percentages of qualifying children, not of every row on the file. It is the strengths-side equivalent of DV1FLAG, and filtering on it before averaging OT1 is the difference between the published rate and a number that merely resembles it.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1Flag'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indicates if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of on one or more domains","k":"Denominator qualification flag for OT1 (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1Flag'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It does not say why a child was excluded. The AEDC's exclusion rules cover children with diagnosed special needs, children aged three and children with too many unanswered instrument items, and all three land on the same zero, so SPECIALNEEDS, the age columns and the five domain validity columns are needed to tell them apart.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"OT2","d":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as \"On Track - On two or more domains\".","full":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as \"On Track - On two or more domains\". It is one of the four sub-threshold companions to OT5, created in 2024 so the whole on-track ladder is calculated the way the national indicators are, and it is reported over the OT2FLAG denominator rather than over all rows. The 2009 to 2015 files hold the older ONTRACK2 in its place.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is developmentally on track on two or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC on-track summary indicator (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from how many of the five domain category columns place the child above the 25th percentile.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"The AEDC publishes no two-or-more on-track rate, so a figure from this column cannot be checked against a national report. It is also not the mirror of DV2: DV2 counts vulnerability on two or more domains, and a child can be flagged on both columns at once.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"OT2FLAG","d":"Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-two-or-more rate.","full":"Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-two-or-more rate. The dictionary defines it as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT2\", introduced in 2024 alongside OT2 itself when the legacy ONTRACK series was rebuilt with explicit denominators. Each on-track threshold has its own flag, so this one qualifies a child for OT2 and for nothing else.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2Flag'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indicates if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of on two or more domains","k":"Denominator qualification flag for OT2 (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2Flag'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"A denominator flag is not a data-quality flag for the whole row. A child excluded here can still have usable domain scores, geography and demographics, so dropping records on this flag discards analysis that has nothing to do with the summary indicator.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"OT3","d":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as \"On Track - On three or more domains\".","full":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as \"On Track - On three or more domains\". It sits in the middle of the OT1 to OT5 ladder introduced for the 2024 collection, and like the rest of that ladder it is meant to be averaged only over children whose matching flag, OT3FLAG, equals 1. Its 2009 to 2015 predecessor is ONTRACK3.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is developmentally on track on three or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC on-track summary indicator (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. The thresholds are cumulative, so a child flagged on OT4 or OT5 is also flagged here.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Subtracting the OT4 rate from the OT3 rate does not give the share on track on exactly three domains, because OT3FLAG and OT4FLAG are separate columns that need not qualify the same children. Nor does the count carry a developmental meaning - each domain has its own cut-off, so moving from three to four is not a fixed increment of development.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"OT3FLAG","d":"Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-three-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT3\".","full":"Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-three-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT3\". It was introduced for the 2024 collection with OT3, part of giving every on-track threshold the kind of explicit denominator the vulnerability indicators had carried since 2009. Without it, an average of OT3 runs over children the AEDC does not count.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3Flag'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indicates if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of on three or more domains","k":"Denominator qualification flag for OT3 (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3Flag'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It qualifies the child for one threshold only, so a denominator built once from this column and reused across OT1 to OT5 will not reproduce the published rates. The dictionary does not publish the qualification rule behind it either, so the flag has to be read from the file rather than rebuilt from the five domain validity columns.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"OT4","d":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as \"On Track - On four or more domains\".","full":"A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as \"On Track - On four or more domains\". It is the closest threshold below OT5, the AEDC's national strengths indicator, and it was created in 2024 when the legacy ONTRACK columns were recalculated onto the OT5 method. Rates need the OT4FLAG denominator.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is developmentally on track on four or more domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC on-track summary indicator (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns rather than from a score.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It is not the opposite of DV1: a child on track on four domains and developmentally vulnerable on the fifth reads 1 on both columns, so the pair cannot be treated as two ends of one scale. It also does not identify which domain the child fell short on, which only the five category columns show.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"OT4FLAG","d":"Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-four-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT4\".","full":"Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-four-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT4\". It is one of the four flags added in 2024 when OT1 to OT4 were created, modelled on DV1FLAG and DV2FLAG so that every AEDC indicator states who it is calculated over. It applies to OT4 only.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4Flag'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indicates if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of on four or more domains","k":"Denominator qualification flag for OT4 (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4Flag'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It is not interchangeable with DV1FLAG or DV2FLAG. The strengths and vulnerability denominators were aligned in method rather than merged, so each indicator keeps its own flag and a single 'valid children' total cannot serve both families of indicators.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"OT5","d":"The AEDC's national strengths measure: a yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on every one of the five domains.","full":"The AEDC's national strengths measure: a yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on every one of the five domains. The dictionary calls it the third summary indicator and describes it as \"a strength-based indicator\" beside the two vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2, and it was created in 2021 so that the strengths measure would be calculated the same way they are. It is the variable behind the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap tracking, and rates must be taken over children with OT5FLAG equal to 1.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5' and section 3.2","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child is developmentally on track on all five domains","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC On Track on Five national summary indicator (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. Like the vulnerability indicators it has no score and no cut-off of its own, resting on whether the child is on track on each domain separately.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5' and section 3.2","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It is not the opposite of DV1. A child who is at risk rather than vulnerable on one domain reads 0 here and 0 on DV1, so the two indicators leave a middle group neither counts and one minus the OT5 rate is not the vulnerability rate. Results from 2018 onward also cannot be joined to ONTRACK5 in the 2009 to 2015 files, which uses the superseded calculation.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"OT5FLAG","d":"Marks whether the child counts in the denominator of the on-track-on-all-five rate, the AEDC's national strengths indicator.","full":"Marks whether the child counts in the denominator of the on-track-on-all-five rate, the AEDC's national strengths indicator. The dictionary defines it as \"Qualifies for the denominator of OT5\" and records it as created in 2021 with OT5 itself, so that the strengths measure would carry the same kind of qualification rule as DV1FLAG and DV2FLAG. It is the flag the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap tracking rests on, so an OT5 rate calculated without it will not match the published series.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5Flag' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indicates if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of on track on all five domains","k":"Denominator qualification flag for OT5 (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5Flag' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It is not a general statement that the child has five usable domain scores; that is what VALIDDOMAINS counts. It is too large to list here; see the value source.","p":"2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables (accompanying workbook), Australian Government Department of Education, Table 1.2 AEDC Country Codeframe (based on the ABS Standard Australian Classification of Countries)","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables.xlsx?sfvrsn=75ae30bf_1","lim":"The source defines the value domain but it is not listed here. Generated values follow the published format rather than the published list.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"PARENT1GENDER","d":"The recorded gender of the adult listed first on the child's school enrolment, pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument.","full":"The recorded gender of the adult listed first on the child's school enrolment, pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument. It identifies whichever adult the school listed first, which need not be a mother, a birth parent or an adult living with the child. With PARENT2GENDER it is the only signal in the AEDC core file about the adults around the child, and it appears from the 2018 cycle onward.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Gender'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"First parent or carer gender","k":"Gender of first listed parent or carer (school enrolment)","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 Male, 2 Female, 9 Not stated. There is no non-binary category and no code separating a refusal from an unrecorded value.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Gender'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It cannot identify family structure. A missing PARENT2GENDER can mean one adult on the enrolment form, a school that recorded only one contact, or a second adult whose details were withheld, and none of those is the same as a single-parent household.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"PARENT1OCCUP","d":"The occupation group of the first adult on the child's enrolment, in the four broad bands Australian schools collect at enrolment.","full":"The occupation group of the first adult on the child's enrolment, in the four broad bands Australian schools collect at enrolment. The dictionary runs them from group 1, \"Senior management in large business organisation, government administration and defence, and qualified professionals\", down to group 4, \"Machine operators, hospitality staff, assistants, labourers and related workers\", with 8 for not in paid work in the last 12 months and 9 for not stated. It is pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument, and it exists only from the 2021 cycle.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Occup'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Occupation group of first parent or carer","k":"School enrolment parental occupation group (four bands)","def":"A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 or 9. It is a broad skill-level grouping rather than an ANZSCO code, so it cannot be resolved to an occupation title or an industry.","p":"2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Occup'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Code 8 is not unemployment: it covers anyone not in paid work in the previous twelve months, including carers, students and retirees, and it sits outside the 1-to-4 order rather than below group 4. Because the value is copied from the enrolment form, it also describes the adult's work when the child enrolled, which can be a year or more before the assessment.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"PARENT1POSTSCHOOL","d":"The highest post-school qualification held by the first adult on the child's enrolment, in four broad bands from a bachelor degree down to none.","full":"The highest post-school qualification held by the first adult on the child's enrolment, in four broad bands from a bachelor degree down to none. The dictionary gives the collection wording as \"What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1\" and records the column as available in both the Complete and Core files, while PARENT1SCHOOL is listed for the Complete file only. PARENT2POSTSCHOOL holds the same measure for the second adult.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1PostSchool'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Post-school qualification of first parent or carer","t":"categorical","k":"Highest post-school qualification, first parent or carer","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 Bachelor degree or above, 2 Advanced Diploma or Diploma, 3 Certificate level I to IV including trade qualification, 4 No post-school qualification, 88 Not known.","p":"2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1PostSchool'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Code 4 is a substantive answer and 88 is the missing one, so pooling them turns parents whose qualification was not recorded into parents with none. The bands also run a Certificate I and a Certificate IV together, which covers a wide range of labour-market positions inside a single code.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"PARENT1SCHOOL","d":"The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the adult listed first on the child's enrolment, banded into four levels.","full":"The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the adult listed first on the child's enrolment, banded into four levels. The dictionary gives the collection wording as \"What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1\", so the answer comes from the enrolment form rather than from the teacher. PARENT1POSTSCHOOL holds the same adult's post-school qualification, and the two must be read together because a parent with a degree still records a school year here.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1School'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"School level completed by first parent or carer","t":"categorical","k":"Highest school year completed, first parent or carer","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 Year 12 or equivalent, 2 Year 11, 3 Year 10, 4 Year 9 or equivalent or below, 88 Not known.","p":"2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1School'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"The scale runs backwards, so a higher code means less schooling and any model that treats the raw code as an education score inverts the result. 'Parent or carer 1' is also only the first adult on the enrolment form, so this is not the mother's education, the resident parent's education or the higher of the two.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"PARENT2GENDER","d":"The recorded gender of the second adult on the child's school enrolment, present only where the school listed a second parent or carer.","full":"The recorded gender of the second adult on the child's school enrolment, present only where the school listed a second parent or carer. Like the first-parent column it is pre-populated from enrolment rather than collected by the AEDC, so it follows whatever the school held rather than the child's living arrangements when the instrument was completed. Paired with PARENT1GENDER it is sometimes used to approximate two-parent or same-sex households, which the AEDC does not itself measure.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Gender'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Second parent or carer gender","k":"Gender of second listed parent or carer (school enrolment)","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 Male, 2 Female, 9 Not stated. The value is absent rather than zero where no second adult was recorded.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Gender'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"This is the weakest basis in the file for inferring household type: a 9 and an absent second parent look similar in analysis but mean different things, and neither confirms who lived with the child. The AEDC records no relationship, so 'parent or carer 2' can be a grandparent, a step-parent or another guardian.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"PARENT2OCCUP","d":"The occupation group of the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column.","full":"The occupation group of the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify the occupation of the second parent or carer\" and records the source as pre-population from the enrolment record, so it is not something the teacher supplied. It appears only in the 2021 and 2024 cycle tables, the shortest history of any parent column in the AEDC core file.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Occup'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Occupation group of second parent or carer","k":"School enrolment parental occupation group (four bands)","def":"A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 or 9, with 8 meaning not in paid work in the last 12 months and 9 not stated.","p":"2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Occup'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It cannot be combined with PARENT1OCCUP into a single household measure without a rule for codes 8 and 9, which are unordered and much more common on the second parent. With only two cycles it also cannot support a trend, and any 2021-to-2024 movement in the distribution may reflect how schools recorded enrolments rather than what parents do.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"PARENT2POSTSCHOOL","d":"The highest post-school qualification held by the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column.","full":"The highest post-school qualification held by the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives the collection wording as \"What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 2\", available from the 2015 cycle in both the Complete and Core files. It is the second half of the AEDC's only measure of parental education.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2PostSchool'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Post-school qualification of second parent or carer","t":"categorical","k":"Highest post-school qualification, second parent or carer","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 Bachelor degree or above, 2 Advanced Diploma or Diploma, 3 Certificate level I to IV including trade qualification, 4 No post-school qualification, 88 Not known.","p":"2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2PostSchool'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Reducing the two parents to a household maximum needs an explicit rule for 88, which is common on the second parent and is not an education level at all. Because the column is absent whenever the school listed only one adult, a household maximum built naively is systematically higher for children with two recorded adults.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"PARENT2SCHOOL","d":"The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the second adult on the child's enrolment, using the same four bands as the first-parent column.","full":"The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the second adult on the child's enrolment, using the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives the collection wording as \"What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 2\", and the column is available from the 2015 cycle onward. It is missing far more often than PARENT1SCHOOL, because it depends on the school holding details for a second adult.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2School'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"School level completed by second parent or carer","t":"categorical","k":"Highest school year completed, second parent or carer","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 Year 12 or equivalent, 2 Year 11, 3 Year 10, 4 Year 9 or equivalent or below, 88 Not known.","p":"2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2School'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"A gap here is not evidence of a single-parent household: the AEDC has no household composition column, so an unrecorded second adult and a genuinely absent one look identical. Taking the better-educated of the two parents also biases toward children whose enrolment happened to list two adults, since the comparison is only possible where both are present.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":19},{"n":"PHNCODE","d":"The Primary Health Network covering the child's home address, held as a code.","full":"The Primary Health Network covering the child's home address, held as a code. The dictionary's file metadata gives it as \"Primary Health Network code: Based on PHN_CODE 2015\", so the 2015 network set is applied to every cycle, and PHNNAME on the same row is the label for the same code. It exists so AEDC results can be lined up with the areas that commission primary health services, which none of the ASGS columns match.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNCode' and Appendix 1; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Primary health network code: based on phn_code 2015","t":"categorical","k":"Primary Health Network code (PHN_CODE 2015)","def":"Six-character text of the form PHNnnn, listed in Table 5.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables. PHN000 is 'Not available' rather than a real network.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNCode' and Appendix 1; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","lim":"It is the network for where the child lives, not where the child is treated and not where the school sits, and the three can differ. The assignment also comes from a concordance between SA1s and PHNs which the Department has since corrected, because \"a small number of SA1s that span across multiple PHNs were re-assigned\", so an older extract can carry the wrong network for those areas.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":37},{"n":"PHNNAME","d":"The name of the Primary Health Network covering the child's home address, carried beside PHNCODE so the row reads without a lookup.","full":"The name of the Primary Health Network covering the child's home address, carried beside PHNCODE so the row reads without a lookup. The dictionary's metadata gives it as \"Primary Health Network name: Based on PHN_CODE 2015\", which shows the name is derived from the same 2015 code rather than assigned independently. Table 5.1 of the reference workbook holds the full code-to-name pairing.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNName' and Appendix 1; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Primary health network name: based on phn_code 2015","t":"categorical","k":"Primary Health Network name (PHN_CODE 2015)","def":"Text up to 44 characters taking one of the PHN names in the reference table, with 'Not available' where no network could be assigned.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNName' and Appendix 1; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","lim":"A name is a weaker join key than a code. Any relabelling of a network leaves the code intact but changes the text, so matching AEDC rows to external health data on the name risks unmatched rows where PHNCODE would have matched; and neither column tells you whether the child's care actually occurs in that network.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":38},{"n":"PHNPUBLIC","d":"Says whether AEDC results for the child's Primary Health Network may be published, and names the reason when they may not.","full":"Says whether AEDC results for the child's Primary Health Network may be published, and names the reason when they may not. The dictionary lists 1 for \"PHN has AEDC results publicly available\" and then five suppression reasons: fewer than 80 per cent of all non-special-needs children, location not available, fewer than 15 valid AEDC children, fewer than two teachers, and the last two together. It is an attribute of the network repeated on every child in it, so it constrains reporting rather than describing the child.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNPublic'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Phn reportability indicator","k":"AEDC reportability indicator for a Primary Health Network","def":"An integer taking 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 or 23, where 1 is publishable and the rest are named suppression reasons.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNPublic'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It restricts publication, not analysis, and it is not a quality flag for the child: a child in a suppressed network has the same valid domain scores as anyone else. Because the indicator is computed on whichever network the child was assigned to, the corrected SA1-to-PHN concordance the Department later issued can move both the assignment and the publishability of small networks.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"PHYS","d":"The child's score on the physical health and wellbeing domain, built from the teacher's answers about gross and fine motor skills, physical independence and readiness for the school day.","full":"The child's score on the physical health and wellbeing domain, built from the teacher's answers about gross and fine motor skills, physical independence and readiness for the school day. The dictionary defines the element as \"Physical health and wellbeing\", records it as derived, and states that for each domain children receive \"a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development\". PHYSCATEGORY turns this score into a percentile band and PHYSVALID says whether it should be used at all.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYS' and section 3.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Physical health and wellbeing","k":"AEDC physical health and wellbeing domain score (0 to 10)","def":"A number between 0 and 10 held to four decimal places, calculated only where at least 75 per cent of the domain's instrument items were completed. The calculation itself is licensed from the Offord Centre at McMaster University and is not published.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYS' and section 3.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"It is not a diagnosis and was not built for the individual child: the dictionary warns that the AEDC indicators \"have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children\" and were validated as population measures. The cut-offs were set on the 2009 population and have not moved since.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYSCategory' and section 3.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Vulnerable - physical health and wellbeing","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain percentile band, physical health and wellbeing","def":"A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3 or 4, defined by fixed percentile cut-offs applied to PHYS. It is the filter to apply before analysing PHYS or PHYSCATEGORY, and each of the five domains has its own version, so a child can be valid on one domain and not another.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYSValid'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Valid - physical health and wellbeing","t":"categorical","k":"Domain validity flag, physical health and wellbeing (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for valid and 0 for not valid. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying a child \"reported as attending a pre-school or kindergarten program in the year before starting school\" and notes it is only answered where instrument item E2 was answered yes, so it depends on the teacher knowing the child's history. PSDC is the broader column that also counts day care, and DAYCARENO is day care without a preschool program.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Preschool'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Attended a pre-school program","t":"categorical","k":"Preschool or kindergarten attendance in the year before school (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying a child \"reported as attending a day care centre or pre-school or kindergarten program in the year before starting school\", so it is the union of PRESCHOOL and DAYCARENO rather than a separate question. Like them it is only answered where instrument item E2 was answered yes.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PSDC'","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Attended day care or pre-school program","t":"categorical","k":"Day care or preschool attendance in the year before school (yes/no)","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 yes, 0 no, 88 'Don't know', which is the AEDC's standard missing-data convention.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PSDC'","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-2025-data-dictionary","lim":"Because it merges formal preschool with day care it cannot support any claim about preschool specifically; that distinction lives in PRESCHOOL and DAYCARENO. The dictionary defines the companion column as \"The AEDC Region where the child lives\", and Table 2.1 of the reference workbook shows the hierarchy this code sits inside: LocalCommunityID within CommunityID within RegionID within StateID. The AEDC publishes results at Local Community, Community, state and national level, and this code identifies the tier those communities are grouped into; no ASGS column reproduces the hierarchy.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entries 'RegionID' and 'Region'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 2.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Region identifier","k":"AEDC Region code (AEDC community geography)","def":"A three-digit integer keyed to Table 2.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, where each region carries a name and a state; REGION on the same row is the label.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entries 'RegionID' and 'Region'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 2.1","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","lim":"The boundaries are not fixed history. The community geography this code sits above was rebuilt for the 2024 collection and \"applied retrospectively to all previous collections\", so a region's 2009 figures in this file need not match what the AEDC published in 2009. The dictionary's file metadata gives it as \"Remoteness area name: Based on RA_NAME_2021\", so it is the label of REMOTENESSCODE on the same row rather than a separate classification. Unlike the code it carries no state digit, so grouping on it gives the five national classes directly.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'Remoteness'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.3","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Remoteness area","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 Remoteness Area name","def":"Text up to 38 characters taking one of the five ASGS 2021 Remoteness Area names or 'Not available', as listed in Table 3.3 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'Remoteness'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.3","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","lim":"It describes where the child lives, not the journey to school or the school's own remoteness, which differ in border areas and wherever children travel to a regional centre. Because the 2021 boundaries are applied to all six cycles, a community that became less remote over time will show the same class in every cycle.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":30},{"n":"REMOTENESSCODE","d":"The ABS remoteness class of the child's home address, held as a two-digit code whose first digit is the state.","full":"The ABS remoteness class of the child's home address, held as a two-digit code whose first digit is the state. The dictionary's metadata gives it as \"Remoteness area code: Based on RA_CODE_2021\", and Table 3.3 of the reference workbook shows the pattern: 10 to 14 run Major Cities through Very Remote in New South Wales, 20 to 24 do the same in Victoria, and so on. SA2NAME is its label and SA2PUBLIC says whether results for it may be published.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'SA2Code'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.1","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/resources/detail/aedc-data-dictionary-reference-tables","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SA2 code","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"The ASGS 2021 SA2 code, published with its SA1, SA3, SA4, GCCSA and state in Table 3.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, where it is listed in nine-digit form; the dictionary's own field format for the column says five digits, so check the width before joining. The dictionary defines it as a code that distinguishes each participating school \"without providing any identifying information\", so it is an arbitrary key rather than a national school number - SCHOOLAGEID is the Australian Government identifier. The dictionary puts it as \"A school is assigned to a state or territory based on geographic location\", which makes it a property of the school rather than of the child: STATE on the same row is where the child lives, and the dictionary notes that \"most published AEDC information uses the variable State (state in which child resides) not SchoolState\". It sits with SCHOOLID, SCHOOLTYPE and TEACHERID as the school-side block of the core table, and it is one of the few school fields released on the linkage version of the file.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SchoolState","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"School state","k":"State or territory abbreviation (three-character text)","def":"Three characters of left-justified text drawn from a closed list of eight: ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC and WA. The dictionary defines it as \"Each school in Australia is classified as Government, Independent or Catholic, depending on the type of governance they operate under\", the standard three-sector split used across Australian schooling statistics. Because AEDC participation is close to a census of that year level, the distribution of this column is a rough picture of where five-year-olds start school, and it is the field used with SEIFACATEGORY and REMOTENESS to describe the schooling context a child's domain scores were reported in.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SchoolType","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"School type","t":"categorical","k":"Australian school sector (governance type)","def":"One character of left-justified text: C for Catholic, G for Government and I for Independent.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SchoolType","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Sector is not fee level, religious character or funding mix.
