It also describes the school, not the child's earlier care, which PRESCHOOL, DAYCARE and PSDC carry.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":41},{"n":"SEIFACATEGORY","d":"The national disadvantage quintile of the small area the child lives in, which the dictionary states as \"SEIFA – IRSD category (quintile) within Australia\".","full":"The national disadvantage quintile of the small area the child lives in, which the dictionary states as \"SEIFA – IRSD category (quintile) within Australia\". The underlying measure is the ABS Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage computed from Census data for the child's Statistical Area Level 1, so it describes the neighbourhood and not the household. It is the socio-economic field carried in every AEDC cycle table here, where SEIFADECILE and SEIFAPERCENTILE appear only from the 2018 file onward, and it is distinct from LCABSSEIFACATEGORY, which reports SEIFA for the much larger AEDC local community, built by population-weighted averaging of the component area scores.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFACategory","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"SEIFA category","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA IRSD quintile, national, at SA1","def":"A single-digit integer from 1 to 5, where 1 is quintile 1 (most disadvantaged) and 5 is quintile 5 (least disadvantaged); the dictionary declares the field as an eight-length integer.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFACategory","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A quintile of an area is not a measure of a family, and many children in the most advantaged quintile live in poor households, so reading category 1 as 'this child is disadvantaged' is the ecological fallacy the ABS warns against. The quintiles are also cut nationally, so a state where few areas fall in quintile 1 has fewer children in that category by geography rather than by need, and the cut points move between SEIFA releases rather than between cycles: the dictionary records the 2011 SEIFA behind the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles, the 2016 SEIFA behind 2018, and the 2021 SEIFA behind both 2021 and 2024.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":29},{"n":"SEIFADECILE","d":"The national disadvantage decile of the small area the child lives in, given by the dictionary as \"SEIFA – IRSD decile within Australia\", and a finer cut of the ranking SEIFACATEGORY holds in quintiles.","full":"The national disadvantage decile of the small area the child lives in, given by the dictionary as \"SEIFA – IRSD decile within Australia\", and a finer cut of the ranking SEIFACATEGORY holds in quintiles. The ABS builds it by ordering every Statistical Area Level 1 by its IRSD score and splitting the ordered list into ten equal groups, so the value is a position in the national distribution rather than a quantity. In this registry it appears only in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables, alongside SEIFAPERCENTILE and SEIFARANK, which is why an analysis spanning all six cycles has to fall back on SEIFACATEGORY.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFADecile","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Seifa - irsd decile within australia","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA IRSD decile, national, at SA1","def":"A two-digit integer from 1 to 10. The ABS assigns it by rank: \"All areas are ordered from lowest to highest score, the lowest 10% of areas are given a decile number of one...up to the highest 10% of areas which are given a decile number of 10\", so 1 is the most disadvantaged tenth.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFADecile","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Deciles are ranks, so the gap between decile 1 and decile 2 is not the same amount of disadvantage as the gap between decile 5 and decile 6, and averaging them produces a number with no interpretation. The decile also comes from the SEIFA release the dictionary assigns to the cycle, the 2016 SEIFA for 2018 and the 2021 SEIFA for both 2021 and 2024, so an area that keeps the same decile across cycles has kept its position relative to other areas rather than its circumstances.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":42},{"n":"SEIFAEXCLUDED","d":"A marker that the child's small area has no SEIFA score to report, which the dictionary describes as denoting \"SEIFA – Denotes unavailability of SEIFA data in particular statistical areas\".","full":"A marker that the child's small area has no SEIFA score to report, which the dictionary describes as denoting \"SEIFA – Denotes unavailability of SEIFA data in particular statistical areas\". It exists because the ABS does not score every Statistical Area Level 1: published exclusion rules drop areas with no or very small populations, with very few employed people or classifiable private dwellings, and with most people counted in non-private dwellings, and those areas are left without an index value. Read it before using SEIFASCORE, SEIFACATEGORY, SEIFADECILE or SEIFAPERCENTILE, since it is the column that tells you an empty or implausible value there is a deliberate absence rather than a data fault.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAExcluded","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"SEIFA excluded flag","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA unavailability flag (single-character text)","def":"A single character of left-justified text. The dictionary declares the format but publishes no code list, so the specific letter or letters used to mark exclusion are not documented.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAExcluded","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It does not say which exclusion rule applied, and the rules differ in what they imply: a tiny population is a statistical limit, while an area where most people live in non-private dwellings is a coverage problem that may itself correlate with disadvantage. Excluded areas are also not spread evenly across the country, so dropping these children removes a clustered group rather than a random slice.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"SEIFAPERCENTILE","d":"The child's small area placed in the national disadvantage ranking to the nearest hundredth, described by the dictionary as \"SEIFA – IRSD percentile within Australia\".","full":"The child's small area placed in the national disadvantage ranking to the nearest hundredth, described by the dictionary as \"SEIFA – IRSD percentile within Australia\". It is the finest of the three ranked SEIFA columns in the AEDC file, with SEIFADECILE grouping the same ordering into tenths and SEIFACATEGORY into fifths, and it is the one to use when a study needs a continuous area-disadvantage control without depending on the score's scale. Like the decile, it appears only in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables here.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAPercentile","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seifa - irsd percentile within australia","k":"SEIFA IRSD percentile, national, at SA1","def":"A three-digit integer from 1 to 100. The ABS forms it by ordering all areas by score, so \"the lowest 1% of areas are given a percentile number of one...up to the highest 1% of areas which are given a percentile number of 100\".","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAPercentile","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Because it is a rank, an area can shift many percentiles between cycles without its own circumstances changing, purely because other areas moved. It also cannot be compared with the percentile of a different SEIFA index or a different geography: a percentile computed over SA1s is not the same yardstick as one computed over suburbs or local government areas.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"SEIFARANK","d":"Seifa - irsd rank within australia","vp":"ai","od":"Seifa - irsd rank within australia","k":"seifa_irsd_rank (integer rank, 1 to about 57,000 (rank of the child's SA1 on the SEIFA IRSD within Australia; 1 = lowest score = most disadvantaged))","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"guessed","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education (SEIFARank, SEIFAScore) and ABS SEIFA 2021","lim":"The value domain is inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"SEIFASCORE","d":"The underlying disadvantage index value for the child's neighbourhood, which the dictionary defines as the \"SEIFA – IRSD score based on the SA1 in which the child lives\".","full":"The underlying disadvantage index value for the child's neighbourhood, which the dictionary defines as the \"SEIFA – IRSD score based on the SA1 in which the child lives\". The ABS builds the Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage from Census variables such as low income, low educational attainment, unemployment and crowded dwellings, then rescales the result, so a lower score means more disadvantage. In this asset the column is present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables only; the later cycles carry the ranked forms in SEIFARANK, SEIFADECILE and SEIFAPERCENTILE instead.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAScore","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"SEIFA score","k":"SEIFA IRSD index score at SA1","def":"A numeric field declared as 12.8, so up to eight decimal places. The ABS standardises index scores across all scored areas: \"We then rescale the raw scores to a mean of 1,000 and standard deviation of 100 to create a new set of scores that are the index scores in SEIFA.\"","p":"2009, 2012, 2015","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAScore","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The scale is set within each SEIFA release, so a score of 950 in the 2011-based index and 950 in the 2016-based index describe a similar position among areas of their day, not the same living conditions. The three cycles that carry this column all draw on the 2011 SEIFA, so a difference in score between them reflects a different area rather than a change in an area's circumstances. The index also summarises disadvantage only, so a high score is an absence of measured disadvantage rather than evidence of advantage, which is a separate ABS index.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core"]},{"n":"SOC","d":"The child's social competence score, one of the five AEDC domain scores a teacher's instrument responses are reduced to.","full":"The child's social competence score, one of the five AEDC domain scores a teacher's instrument responses are reduced to. The dictionary states that \"AEDC domain scores are calculated based on teacher responses to the relevant domain questions for each child\", and for this domain the questions are the twenty-four C-series items C1 to C23 and C25, covering overall social competence, responsibility and respect, approaches to learning, and readiness to explore new things; the sub-domain scores SOC_1 to SOC_4 report those four strands separately. Two columns qualify it on the same row: SOCVALID says whether the score should be used at all, and SOCCATEGORY places it in the percentile band that turns it into the published vulnerable, at-risk and on-track categories.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOC and section 3.1 Domain Indicators","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Social competence","k":"AEDC domain score, 0 to 10 (social competence)","def":"A numeric field declared as 7.4, so four decimal places. The dictionary gives its purpose as \"To identify the grouping variable for the cumulative frequency of scores in the social competence domain\", and it is the column that produces published AEDC reporting: band 1 is developmentally vulnerable on this domain, band 2 is developmentally at risk, and bands 3 and 4 are on track. The column is also not calculated for every child, since categories are only produced where the domain score is valid, which excludes children with special needs status and children aged three.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":0},{"n":"SOCVALID","d":"Whether this child's social competence result may be used, which the dictionary states as being \"To identify the validity of the child's results on the social competence domain\".","full":"Whether this child's social competence result may be used, which the dictionary states as being \"To identify the validity of the child's results on the social competence domain\". It is the gate on SOC and SOCCATEGORY: a child can carry a stored score while this column says the score does not qualify for reporting. Each of the five domains has its own flag of this shape, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of them are set to 1 for the child.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCValid","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Valid - social competence","t":"categorical","k":"AEDC domain validity flag (0 or 1)","def":"A single-digit integer: 1 where the child \"does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain\", and 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCValid","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A 0 does not tell you which of its three causes applied, so it cannot be used as a measure of item non-response; SPECIALNEEDS and the age fields have to be checked to separate a child excluded by rule from one whose teacher left questions blank. It is also a statement about this domain only, not about the instrument as a whole, which is what VALIDINSTRUMENT covers.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"SPECIALNEEDS","d":"Whether the teacher recorded the child as having special needs status when completing the instrument.","full":"Whether the teacher recorded the child as having special needs status when completing the instrument. The Data Guidelines define the term as applying to \"children reported by teachers as requiring special assistance because of chronic medical, physical, or intellectually disabling conditions (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome) based on a medical diagnosis or diagnoses\". The value governs most of the rest of the record: children flagged 1 are counted in the AEDC population, but their domain results are ruled invalid and their domain categories are not calculated, which is why the published denominators, and the 80 per cent coverage rule that VALIDINSTRUMENT serves, count only children with SPECIALNEEDS = 0.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Guidelines (Australian Government Department of Education, 2025), glossary entry Special needs, with the code frame in the AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 entry SpecialNeeds","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/aedc-data-guidelines.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Special needs status","t":"categorical","k":"Teacher-reported special needs status (0 or 1)","def":"A single-digit integer: 0 for not special needs and 1 for special needs. The item is asked of the teacher as \"Is this child considered Special Needs\".","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Guidelines (Australian Government Department of Education, 2025), glossary entry Special needs, with the code frame in the AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 entry SpecialNeeds","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/aedc-data-guidelines.pdf","lim":"It is the teacher's report at the time of the collection, made against a medical diagnosis but recorded through school processes, so the share flagged is not a prevalence estimate for disability and should not be compared between jurisdictions without care. It also says nothing about the condition itself, which the D-series items on the AEDC special needs table carry.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":2},{"n":"STATE","d":"The state or territory the child lives in, given by the dictionary as \"The state or territory in which the child resides\" and derived rather than reported directly by the teacher.","full":"The state or territory the child lives in, given by the dictionary as \"The state or territory in which the child resides\" and derived rather than reported directly by the teacher. It is the jurisdiction field AEDC reporting actually uses, and the dictionary says so explicitly: most published AEDC information uses this column and not SCHOOLSTATE. STATEID on the same row is the numeric form of the same fact, and the geography chain below it runs through REGION, LOCALCOMMUNITY, LGA and the ABS statistical areas.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry State","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State or territory","k":"State or territory abbreviation (three-character text)","def":"Three characters of left-justified text from the same closed eight-value list as SCHOOLSTATE: ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC and WA.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry State","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"Because it is derived from the child's recorded address at the time of the collection, it is a point-in-time residence and not a history: a child who moved interstate between school enrolment and the instrument is placed where they were when the record was built. It is also not the jurisdiction responsible for the child's schooling, which is SCHOOLSTATE and can differ near borders.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"STATEELECTORATE","d":"State electoral division: based on sed_name_2021","vp":"ai","od":"State electoral division: based on sed_name_2021","k":"asgs2021_sed_name","def":"The source publishes this value domain of 433 values. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"STATEELECTORATEPUBLIC","d":"Whether AEDC results may be published for the state electoral division the child lives in, and if not, which rule stopped them.","full":"Whether AEDC results may be published for the state electoral division the child lives in, and if not, which rule stopped them. The dictionary describes the field as the \"SED reportability indicator\" and prints six codes, one meaning publishable and five naming a specific failure: too few valid children, too few teachers, both, coverage below 80 per cent of non-special-needs children, or no location. It is the electorate member of a family of publication codes that also covers communities (CPUBLIC), local communities (LCPUBLIC), Indigenous areas (IAREPUBLIC) and statistical areas, and it appears in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables only.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateElectoratePublic","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sed reportability indicator","k":"AEDC state electoral division publication reason code","def":"A single-digit stored value drawn from six codes: 1 publicly available; 5 less than 80 per cent of all non-special-needs children; 9 location not available; 21 fewer than 15 valid AEDC children; 22 fewer than two teachers; 23 both fewer than 15 valid children and fewer than two teachers.","p":"2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateElectoratePublic","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is a rule about reporting an area, not a judgement on the child: a code of 21 or 22 does not mean this row is unreliable, only that the electorate it belongs to is too thin to report. It also carries nothing about which electoral boundaries applied, so it cannot be used to align a cycle's results with a particular redistribution; STATEELECTORATECODE and STATEELECTORATE hold the identity of the division.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"STATEID","d":"The numeric code for the state or territory the child lives in, which the dictionary states as a \"Code for state in which child resides\".","full":"The numeric code for the state or territory the child lives in, which the dictionary states as a \"Code for state in which child resides\". It is the join key at the top of the AEDC's own geography hierarchy, which runs state, region, community and local community, so it pairs with REGIONID, COMMUNITYID and LOCALCOMMUNITYID rather than with any ABS geography code. STATE on the same row carries the same fact as a three-letter abbreviation, and the reference tables that publish the code list are also what expands REGIONID and LOCALCOMMUNITYID.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateID, with the codes in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 2.1 AEDC Geography","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State identifier","k":"AEDC state and territory code (1 to 8)","def":"A single-digit integer running 1 to 8 in the ABS jurisdiction order: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory. The dictionary defers the list to the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, where Table 2.1 carries it against every AEDC local community.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateID, with the codes in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 2.1 AEDC Geography","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is not an ABS state code in the sense of the ASGS state and territory structure, which carries a further code for Other Territories: the dictionary records that the AEDC does not use that designation and assigns those places to the nearest jurisdiction, so Cocos and Christmas Islands fall under Western Australia and Jervis Bay and Norfolk Island under New South Wales. It also identifies the child's residence, so it will not reconcile with a school-based count built on SCHOOLSTATE.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"SYNTHETIC_AEUID","d":"The person key that ties a child's AEDC record to the rest of PLIDA, and the reason the collection is in this asset at all.","full":"The person key that ties a child's AEDC record to the rest of PLIDA, and the reason the collection is in this asset at all. Within AEDC it joins the five tables of a cycle, so a child's core record, domain scores, instrument background, language detail and special needs detail assemble on this column; across the asset it is the same key the Census, births, MBS, PBS, DOMINO and the tax products carry, so an AvEDI result can be read against a child's birth record, health history or family's payment history. ABS lists the AEDC among PLIDA's linked sources, naming the 2009, 2012, 2015 and 2018 collections on its data page while this asset carries six cycles, and the linkage is performed centrally against the person linkage spine rather than by matching names in this file.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic MADIP Person ID","k":"PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)","def":"A numeric identifier assigned for linkage with no meaning in its digits. It is not a student number, an enrolment identifier or an AEDC instrument identifier, so it can be matched but not decoded.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida/plida-data-and-legislation","lim":"A child appears here only where their AvEDI record linked to the spine, and children who did not link are missing rather than untested, so AEDC coverage in PLIDA is lower than AEDC coverage in the national collection and the shortfall should not be assumed random. The key is also for the child, not the class or the family: TEACHERID and SCHOOLID group the record, and no parent or sibling identifier is carried, so a family cannot be assembled from this column alone.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2009 / aedc_2009_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2012 / aedc_2012_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2015 / aedc_2015_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2018 / aedc_2018_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2021 / aedc_2021_dom","madipge-aedc-d-domain-2024 / aedc_2024_dom","and 18 more"]},{"n":"TEACHERATSI","d":"Whether the teacher who completed the instrument identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, asked directly as \"Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent\".","full":"Whether the teacher who completed the instrument identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, asked directly as \"Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent\". It sits in the instrument background table with the CONSULTTYPE items about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural consultants, and the point of the block is to describe who did the assessing rather than who was assessed. It is the column to use when testing whether teacher background is associated with reported outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, whose own status is on ATSI in the core table.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous teacher","k":"Teacher Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status (three values)","def":"A single-digit integer with three values: 0 the teacher was not Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, 1 the teacher was, and 2 the teacher responded inconsistently to their own Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It describes the teacher, not the child, so it cannot stand in for the child's Indigenous status anywhere. Code 2 is also a data quality state rather than a third identity: it marks contradictory answers within the teacher's own record, so quietly dropping it or folding it into 0 shifts the measured share of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander teachers in an unknown direction.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2009 / aedc_2009_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2012 / aedc_2012_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2015 / aedc_2015_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2018 / aedc_2018_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2021 / aedc_2021_ind","madipge-aedc-d-indigenous-2024 / aedc_2024_ind"]},{"n":"TEACHERID","d":"Which teacher filled in the instrument for this child, as a de-identified number.","full":"Which teacher filled in the instrument for this child, as a de-identified number. The dictionary describes it as a \"unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information\", and its analytic value is as the clustering unit: every AvEDI score is one teacher's judgement of one child, so children sharing a value here share a rater and their scores are not independent observations. SCHOOLID nests these teachers within schools, and CLASSTYPEA_1, CLASSTYPEB and CLASSTYPEC describe the class the teacher was reporting on.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Teacher identifier","k":"AEDC teacher identifier (de-identified)","def":"A right-justified integer, allocated for the collection and carrying no information about the teacher. The dictionary's variable page gives it a length of 11, while its appendix metadata shows the narrower format F6.0.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It is not a person key on the PLIDA spine, so a teacher cannot be joined to their own tax, payment or health records the way a child can through SYNTHETIC_AEUID; nothing about the teacher beyond TEACHERATSI is available. The dictionary also does not state that the code is stable between collections, so it should not be used to follow one teacher from 2009 to a later cycle.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"TMSCH","d":"Whether the child had been in class for less than one month when the instrument was started, and if so whether the teacher went on to fill it in anyway.","full":"Whether the child had been in class for less than one month when the instrument was started, and if so whether the teacher went on to fill it in anyway. The dictionary's reason for asking is that \"If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC\", and the teacher may then stop. This is why a row can exist with almost nothing on it: a value of 1 here is the explanation for empty domain scores and empty instrument items, and CANASSESS, asked only when this is a yes, records whether the teacher felt able to assess the child at all.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"In school for less than one month","t":"categorical","k":"Time in class under one month, with completion intent (three values)","def":"A single-digit integer with three values: 0 no, 1 yes and skip the rest of the instrument, and 2 yes but the rest of the instrument will be completed.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"The instrument asks about time in this class while the dictionary's description speaks of time at school, so a child who transferred in October after a full year elsewhere may be coded the same as a child who started school that month. It is also not a data quality flag on the responses that follow: a 1 means there are no responses to judge, while a 2 means the teacher went ahead on under a month's acquaintance and the scores stand in the file unmarked.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"],"dom":8},{"n":"TOTALMISS","d":"How many of the five AEDC scales could not be calculated for this child, defined by the dictionary as the \"Total number of missing scales (0-5)\".","full":"How many of the five AEDC scales could not be calculated for this child, defined by the dictionary as the \"Total number of missing scales (0-5)\". It is the sum of the five per-scale missing flags PHMiss, SCMiss, EMMiss, LCMiss and CGMiss, which the dictionary restricts to the master unit record file and which are not carried in the AEDC tables in this asset, so this count is the only summary of scale-level missingness available here. A scale goes missing when fewer than 75 per cent of that domain's instrument items were answered.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total number of missing scales (0-5)","k":"Count of missing domain scales (0 to 5)","def":"A single-digit integer from 0 to 5, one unit for each of physical health and wellbeing, social competence, emotional maturity, language and cognitive skills, and communication and general knowledge.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"It does not say which scales are missing, so a value of 2 needs the five domain score columns checked one by one before an analysis can decide whether the loss matters. It is also not the complement of VALIDDOMAINS: a scale can be computed and still be ruled invalid because the child has special needs status or is three years old, so the two columns need not add to five.","where":["madipge-aedc-d-core-2009 / aedc_2009_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2012 / aedc_2012_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2015 / aedc_2015_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2018 / aedc_2018_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2021 / aedc_2021_core","madipge-aedc-d-core-2024 / aedc_2024_core"]},{"n":"VALIDDOMAINS","d":"How many of the five AEDC domains yielded a usable score for this child, which the dictionary gives as being \"To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid\".","full":"How many of the five AEDC domains yielded a usable score for this child, which the dictionary gives as being \"To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid\". It is the total of the five per-domain flags PHYSVALID, SOCVALID, EMOTVALID, LANGCOGVALID and COMGENVALID, and it is the input to the reporting rule: children with fewer than four valid domains are the ones VALIDINSTRUMENT marks as not counting. Use it as the first filter on any analysis of domain scores, ahead of the individual flags.","dsrc":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains","durl":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Valid domains","t":"categorical","k":"Count of valid domain scores (0 to 5)","def":"A single-digit integer from 0 to 5. The dictionary publishes no value labels because the number is simply the count of domains for which the validity conditions were met.","p":"2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021, 2024","s":"sourced","src":"AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains","url":"https://www.aedc.gov.au/docs/default-source/default-document-library/2025-aedc-data-dictionary8b9c155b-5dcb-4621-b7da-8b7830bdec10.pdf","lim":"A 0 does not mean an empty instrument. Children with special needs status have no valid domain scores by rule, so they sit at 0 while their teacher may have answered every question, and reading this column as a response-quality measure conflates an administrative exclusion with missing data.
